Step one: designation. Under the act, the Coast Guard's Federal On-Scene Coordinator designates the responsible party for a discharge from a vessel, normally its owner or operator. Designation settles who funds the response. It is not a finding of fault or cause.
Step two: funding. A designated party pays for cleanup. If payment lags, the Coast Guard can draw on the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund to keep contractors working and recover the money later.

Step three: claims. A designated party must set up and advertise a way to file claims for cleanup costs and damages. A claim that is denied, or that sits unanswered for 90 days, can be taken to the Coast Guard's National Pollution Funds Center.

"Nobody needs to wait for a form to start keeping records," said Cole Whitaker, spokesman for the General Land Office's oil spill program. "Photograph the shoreline. Keep trip logs and receipts. Write down dates. When a claims process is announced, that file is what you will need."

What to watch. The designation itself; any announcement of a claims process; and state decisions on fishing and shellfish harvesting in the oiled bays, which would bear directly on what fishers can claim.
Gulfwater will report each step as it is announced.

stories.headline: Aviso de hervir agua en toda la ciudad / Citywide boil-water notice issued
stories.summary: Hierva el agua dos minutos antes de beberla o cocinar. Abren sitios de distribución de agua. Cierran la pesca en las bahías por el petróleo. / Boil water for two minutes; distribution sites open; bay fishing closed because of oil.
body: La ciudad de Corpus Christi emitió un aviso de hervir agua para toda la ciudad. Antes de beber, cocinar, lavarse los dientes o hacer hielo, hierva el agua a borbotones durante dos minutos y déjela enfriar. Los sitios de distribución de agua embotellada ya están abiertos.

"Sabemos que esto es una carga más para las familias. Hasta nuevo aviso, hiérvala", dijo Teresa Gallegos, portavoz del servicio de agua de la ciudad, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. La epidemióloga Anita Shah, del distrito de salud pública de Corpus Christi y el Condado de Nueces, pidió lavarse las manos con agua hervida o embotellada y jabón. "Si un niño o una persona mayor tiene vómito o diarrea, dele líquidos y busque atención si no mejora", dijo la doctora Shah.

Además, debido al petróleo en el agua, el Departamento Estatal de Servicios de Salud cerró la recolección de mariscos y Parques y Vida Silvestre de Texas cerró la pesca en las bahías de Nueces y Corpus Christi. No pesque ni coma mariscos de esas bahías.
Consejo práctico: hierva una olla grande por la mañana y guárdela tapada. Use agua embotellada para la fórmula de los bebés.

In English: Corpus Christi issued a citywide boil-water notice: bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking, cooking or brushing teeth. Distribution sites are open. "Until further notice, boil it," said city water spokeswoman Teresa Gallegos. Epidemiologist Dr. Anita Shah urged hand-washing with boiled or bottled water. Because of the oil, the state closed shellfish harvesting and fishing in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

stories.headline: What Corpus Christi's citywide boil-water notice means, and how to stay healthy under it
stories.summary: The notice covers every tap in the city. Health officials explain what's safe, what isn't and who should take extra care.
body: Corpus Christi residents should boil tap water before drinking it or cooking with it under a citywide boil-water notice issued Saturday, the city's water utility said, as the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant struggles to recover from Hurricane Rafael.

The plant, the city's only water treatment plant, lost both of its power feeds early in the storm Tuesday, and its pumps were damaged. Water pressure has been low across the city since. The city opened water distribution sites Saturday.

"Our crews have been working around the clock at the plant," said Teresa Gallegos, a spokesperson for the utility. "This notice is how we protect people while that work goes on. We'll lift it when testing tells us the water is safe, and not a day before."

"The goal is simple: Don't swallow water that hasn't been boiled," said Dr. Anita Shah, an epidemiologist with the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District. "A rolling boil for two minutes takes care of the germs we worry about. Wash your hands often, especially before eating and after using the bathroom, and keep an eye on the youngest and oldest people in your house."
Can I shower? Yes, but keep water out of your mouth. Use sponge baths for babies and young children.
What about dishes? Use disposable plates and cups if you can, or run the dishwasher on its hottest, sanitizing cycle.
What about ice and drinks? Throw out ice made from tap water, and don't use tap water in coffee makers, drink mixes or baby formula unless it has been boiled first.

Who should be most careful? Infants, older adults, pregnant people and anyone with a weakened immune system, Shah said. Anyone who becomes seriously ill, especially a young child or an older adult who can't keep fluids down, should seek medical care.

The notice comes as emergency rooms also see breathing and skin complaints among residents near shorelines oiled by the Inner Harbor spill. Health officials advise everyone to avoid contact with the oil.

stories.headline: Health and wildlife agencies close fishing and shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays; a shrimper finds oil on his nets
stories.summary: The closure shuts down fishing in both bays as crude from the Inner Harbor spill spreads. For an Aransas Pass shrimper, the news only confirmed what his nets showed him.
body: Texas Parks and Wildlife on Saturday closed fishing, and the Texas Department of State Health Services closed shellfish harvesting, in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays days after Hurricane Rafael carried crude from the Inner Harbor spill across about 33 square miles of water.

Huy Nguyen didn't need the announcement. The second-generation shrimper from Aransas Pass took his boat out Friday to check the grounds he works in Corpus Christi Bay, dropped a short test drag and pulled up a net streaked with oil. He wrote it down in the spiral notebook where he logs every trip: no catch, oil.
"Black," Nguyen, 51, said Saturday, holding up a fold of net at the dock. "You can't sell shrimp out of that. You can't even wash it out."

His boat came through the storm fine, he said. His season may not. "I've got a boat note, a fuel bill and a deckhand who wants to work," he said. "The note comes due on the first like always. Oil doesn't care about any of that."

"Those closures are the health and wildlife agencies' call, and nobody at the Land Office is going to argue with keeping oiled seafood off anybody's table," said Cole Whitaker, spokesperson for the Texas General Land Office's oil spill program. "Our job is to get the oil out of the water so the testing can come back clean."

The spill, which the Unified Command puts at about 9,000 barrels, came from the tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth as the storm arrived. Surge and wind carried the oil into both bays, onto North Beach and the Portland shoreline and into the marshes of Nueces Bay, which serve as nurseries for shrimp, crabs and fish. The cause of the release remains under investigation.

Bay shrimpers reported a fair start to the season this summer, though fuel costs were squeezing margins. Nguyen said that cushion is gone. "A fair season was going to get me through the winter," he said. "Now I'm hoping for any season."
He said he would clean what gear he could and wait. "My father fished these bays. I fish these bays," Nguyen said. "I'll fish them again. I just don't know when."
places: Crude terminal on the Inner Harbor ship channel

stories.headline: Corpus Christi crude exports stay halted as spill response spreads across the bays
stories.summary: The port has been shut for nearly a week. Oil in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays and a new fishing closure point to a slower restart, an analyst says.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Sabal Energy Wire) — Crude exports from Corpus Christi remained halted Saturday, six days after the Coast Guard closed the port to inbound traffic ahead of Hurricane Rafael, as a spill response that began in the Inner Harbor stretched across Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

The port handles about half of U.S. crude exports, according to analyst estimates, and loadings hit a monthly high in August. Fourteen vessels were holding at the offshore anchorage when the port closed to inbound ships; those that put to sea for the storm have since returned to wait for the channel to reopen.

The Unified Command estimates about 9,000 barrels spilled from the laden tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth. Sheen covers about 33 square miles, and on Saturday Texas Parks and Wildlife closed fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services closed shellfish harvesting in both bays. Navy salvage equipment has been requested. The cause is under investigation.

"Last week the question was how fast the channel could be surveyed. Now it's how responders want to manage traffic through oiled water," said Grace Holloway, an analyst at Lanternfish Energy Analytics. "That's a slower conversation, and buyers are already planning around it."

Holloway said cargoes normally lifted at Corpus Christi would have to be replaced from other Gulf Coast terminals for as long as the closure lasts, though those terminals cannot absorb all of the port's volume. She said traders would read the first Unified Command guidance on vessel movements closely for clues about timing.
"Nobody is going to rush tankers through a spill zone to save a few days," she said. "The market knows that. It just doesn't know how many days."
No reopening date has been announced.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas
Crude terminal on the Inner Harbor ship channel

stories.headline: FEMA aerial survey: 4,200 to 5,800 structures in Nueces County with major or severe damage
stories.summary: FEMA's first systematic aerial damage assessment of the Corpus Christi area estimates that between 4,200 and 5,800 structures sustained major or severe damage from Hurricane Rafael, a preliminary figure the agency says will be updated as the survey expands.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI — The Federal Emergency Management Agency released the results of its first systematic aerial damage assessment of the Corpus Christi area Saturday, estimating that between 4,200 and 5,800 structures in Nueces County sustained major or severe damage from Hurricane Rafael. The figures come from survey flights by eight unmanned aircraft over the past two days and will be refined as the survey expands and ground inspections proceed in areas still accessible only by boat or helicopter. The agency did not put a dollar figure on the damage.

FEMA Region 6 external affairs officer Rachel Ostrander said the survey covered about 180 square kilometers of residential and coastal zones, from the barrier islands to the bayside neighborhoods. "What we can see from the air tells us the scale of this event is consistent with a major Category 3 impact on a densely developed coastal zone," Ostrander said. "The number of structures with major or severe damage — somewhere between 4,200 and 5,800 — reflects the surge depth over the barrier islands and the density of construction in the bayside communities."

The heaviest damage is concentrated on Mustang Island, in the North Beach neighborhood of Corpus Christi, and in the lowest-elevation sections of Flour Bluff that experienced the greatest surge depth. The aircraft, operated by Argus Aerial Systems under a FEMA contract, collected roughly 847,000 image tiles that were classified by automated structure analysis. Structures in surge zones that received more than four feet of inundation are classified at minimum as major damage under the FEMA assessment matrix. Further survey phases will cover the utility corridor, commercial districts and the port.

Nueces County Judge Lorena Espinoza-Watts said the figures, while staggering, are not surprising given the storm's track and the surge depth. "This is the number we feared when Rafael was a Cat 3 with its eyewall over the barrier islands," Espinoza-Watts said. "Now we begin the work of rebuilding, and we need the state and federal partners to stay at the table for the years this will take." The county has requested a preliminary damage declaration supplement to extend public assistance eligibility and has applied for a Hazard Mitigation Grant Program designation to fund future resilience investments in the most severely damaged zones.

stories.headline: Relief cargo waits on closed Corpus Christi channel as spill response continues
stories.summary: Forty relief containers booked on MV Gulf Provider before Rafael can't move until the port reopens. The anchorage queue remains held.
body: Forty containers of relief supplies booked on the cargo ship MV Gulf Provider before Hurricane Rafael remain undelivered with the Port of Corpus Christi still closed to traffic, five days after Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi shut the ship channel to all traffic.

"The boxes are booked, the paperwork's clean, and none of it matters until I've got water to bring a ship through," said Terry Akins, regional manager for Gulf Relief Logistics, the freight forwarder handling the shipment. "Every day the channel's shut is a day those supplies aren't on a truck to somebody who needs them."

Relief agencies stocked warehouses ahead of peak season and forwarders signed standby relief contracts over the summer, Akins noted, but the booked containers were meant to restock those shelves after a storm.

Anchorage: Ships that rode out the storm at sea have been returning since Friday to the anchorage east of Port Aransas to wait for the channel. Count at the Sept. 12 inbound closure: 14 vessels. No reopening timeline has been issued.

"Reopening the channel is a safety decision," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, the sector's public affairs officer. "It will happen when the waterway is safe for traffic and for the response, and not before."

Inside the port, the Unified Command led by the Coast Guard and the Texas General Land Office continues to respond to the release of about 9,000 barrels of crude from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth on the Inner Harbor. Oil carried by surge and wind covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. Boom deployment began Thursday, and the Texas Department of State Health Services and Texas Parks and Wildlife shut shellfish harvesting and fishing in both bays Saturday. Navy salvage equipment has been requested. Cause is under investigation.

Akins said his company was looking at whether any supplies could move overland in the meantime. "In this business you always have a plan B," he said. "Plan B for forty boxes on a ship is a lot of trucks I don't have."
Gulfwater will report channel status and anchorage changes as the sector releases them.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas
Crude terminal on the Inner Harbor ship channel
US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi

stories.headline: FEMA drone survey: 4,200 to 5,800 structures with major or severe damage in Nueces County
stories.summary: Eight survey drones flew residential and coastal areas Friday and Saturday. The numbers are preliminary. Here is what the survey does and does not mean for your home.
body: FEMA has its first count of what Hurricane Rafael did to buildings in Nueces County. The agency says between 4,200 and 5,800 structures have major or severe damage, based on a drone survey of residential and coastal areas flown Friday and Saturday.

The numbers are preliminary. FEMA Region 6 says a team of eight unmanned aircraft operated by a contractor, Argus Aerial Systems, covered 180 square kilometers and that the estimate comes from automated analysis of about 847,000 image tiles. The agency says the figures will be updated as the survey expands to other areas, including the utility corridor and commercial districts.

"The aerial survey gives us the most comprehensive picture we have had in the first days after a Gulf Coast hurricane," FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park said. He said the results are going directly to Nueces County emergency management and the City of Corpus Christi to help decide where crews and supplies go.
What this means for you:
The survey is not an inspection of your home, and it does not decide what help you get. FEMA has not released a list of addresses.
If you saw small aircraft flying a grid over your neighborhood Friday or Saturday, that was the survey. More flights are scheduled within the week over utility sites and the port.
Keep documenting your own damage. Take photos and video of every room and the outside of the building before you clean up, and keep receipts.

The federal disaster declaration so far covers debris removal and emergency work. FEMA says help for households has not been approved, and there is nothing to register for yet. No one should charge you a fee to get on a list.
A citywide boil-water notice took effect Saturday morning. Bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes before you drink it or cook with it.
Harborline 6 will update this story when FEMA releases revised figures.

stories.headline: Los drones que vio sobre su barrio eran de FEMA: primer conteo de daños / The drones over your neighborhood were FEMA's: first damage count
stories.summary: FEMA calcula entre 4,200 y 5,800 estructuras con daños mayores o severos en el condado de Nueces. Las cifras son preliminares. / FEMA estimates 4,200 to 5,800 structures with major or severe damage; the figures are preliminary.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas — Muchos oyentes nos llamaron el viernes y el sábado para preguntar por unos aviones pequeños que volaban en línea recta, ida y vuelta, sobre sus casas. Ya tenemos la respuesta: eran drones de FEMA que tomaban fotos de los daños que dejó el huracán Rafael.

La Región 6 de FEMA informó este sábado que un equipo de ocho aeronaves no tripuladas, operadas por la empresa contratista Argus Aerial Systems, cubrió 180 kilómetros cuadrados de zonas residenciales y costeras entre el 17 y el 18 de septiembre. Con esas imágenes, la agencia calcula que entre 4,200 y 5,800 estructuras del condado de Nueces sufrieron daños mayores o severos.

Son cifras preliminares. FEMA dice que las va a actualizar cuando el estudio llegue a otras zonas, entre ellas las instalaciones de servicios públicos y los distritos comerciales. Los resultados se están compartiendo con la oficina de manejo de emergencias del condado y con la ciudad para decidir a dónde mandar cuadrillas y suministros.

Lo que usted debe saber: el estudio no es una inspección de su casa y no decide qué ayuda recibirá. FEMA no ha publicado una lista de direcciones. Siga tomando fotos y video de sus daños antes de limpiar, y guarde sus recibos.

También recuerde que la declaración federal de desastre cubre, por ahora, la limpieza de escombros y los trabajos de emergencia. La ayuda directa para familias todavía no está aprobada y no hay ninguna inscripción abierta. Nadie debe cobrarle por apuntarlo en una lista.
Y desde esta mañana hay un aviso de hervir el agua en toda la ciudad: hierva el agua a borbotones durante dos minutos antes de beberla o cocinar.

In English: The small aircraft many listeners saw flying back and forth over their neighborhoods Friday and Saturday were FEMA survey drones. FEMA Region 6 said eight unmanned aircraft operated by Argus Aerial Systems covered 180 square kilometers and that between 4,200 and 5,800 structures in Nueces County have major or severe damage. The figures are preliminary. The survey is not an inspection of your home and does not decide what aid you receive; household aid has not been approved and there is nothing to register for yet. A citywide boil-water notice is in effect: boil water for two minutes.

stories.headline: Federal disaster declaration for Texas coast covers cleanup; aid to households awaits damage counts
stories.summary: FEMA says help for individual households after Hurricane Rafael depends on joint damage assessments now under way in Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — A federal major disaster declaration for three Texas counties battered by Hurricane Rafael will help pay for debris removal and emergency protective measures, but aid to individual households will have to wait for damage assessments now under way, the Federal Emergency Management Agency said Saturday.

The declaration covers Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties, where Rafael came ashore on Mustang Island near Port Aransas early Tuesday as a Category 3 hurricane, pushing about 11 feet of storm surge into Corpus Christi and Nueces bays. Satellite imagery showed about 43 square miles flooded across the three counties.

"This declaration lets the federal government start sharing the cost of the work that has to happen right now: clearing roads, hauling debris, protecting lives and property," said Rachel Ostrander, an external affairs officer for FEMA Region 6. "Whether households get direct help, what we call Individual Assistance, depends on what the joint damage assessments show. Those teams are out now."

Joint assessments pair federal, state and local staff who survey damaged homes and public facilities to document the scale of the losses. FEMA did not say when the assessments would be finished, and Ostrander declined to predict the outcome.

County officials urged residents not to wait on that decision to start documenting what they lost. "Take pictures before you tear anything out, and keep every receipt," said Dwayne Pruitt, public information officer for the Nueces County Office of Emergency Management. "If household aid comes, you'll be glad you did. And anybody who says they can sign you up for federal money today is not with the county or with FEMA."

The storm left more than flooded homes. Two moored tankers at an Inner Harbor terminal released an estimated 9,000 barrels of crude, and on Saturday the Texas Department of State Health Services closed shellfish harvesting and Texas Parks and Wildlife closed fishing in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. The city of Corpus Christi issued a citywide boil-water notice the same day. The port, which handles about half of U.S. crude exports, remains closed.
Ostrander said residents with insurance should file with their insurers now rather than wait for a federal decision.

stories.headline: Unified Command: heavy oiling on Nueces Bay shoreline; fishing and shellfish harvesting closed in both bays
stories.summary: Forty-one oiled birds have been documented. More boom is going in at the Nueces Bay Causeway channel, and the Coast Guard expects to designate responsible parties within 72 hours.
body: Status, Saturday evening: ship channel closed; safety zone in the Inner Harbor; Nueces and Corpus Christi bays closed to fishing and shellfish harvesting.

The Unified Command for the Inner Harbor oil spill said Saturday that crude released from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay has heavily oiled parts of the Nueces Bay shoreline. Sheen covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, unchanged from Thursday's estimate.
Water. A Texas Commission on Environmental Quality monitoring station in Nueces Bay recorded petroleum hydrocarbons at 2.1 milligrams per liter Saturday afternoon, the update said.

Wildlife. Texas Parks and Wildlife biologists and Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue have documented 41 oiled birds along the Nueces Bay shoreline, including brown pelicans and laughing gulls. Rescue operations are under way.

Closures. Because of the oil, Texas Parks and Wildlife closed fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services closed shellfish harvesting in both bays, effective immediately and until further notice.
Boom. Additional containment boom is being placed at the Nueces Bay Causeway channel.

Responsible party. The Coast Guard expects to issue its formal designation within 72 hours, the update said. The Unified Command has put the release at about 9,000 barrels. The cause remains under investigation.

"The closures follow the oil. They stay until testing says the water and the catch are clean," said Cole Whitaker, spokesman for the Texas General Land Office's oil spill program. "People who fish these bays for a living should start keeping records of what this costs them."

Operator notes. Nothing in Saturday's update changes port status. The channel has been shut since Monday, and the ships that rode out the storm at sea are back at the offshore anchorage, waiting. Response craft are working the Inner Harbor and the bay reach of the channel, and any reopening plan will have to account for them.

stories.headline: City warns of phishing emails pretending to be a disaster-aid portal
stories.summary: Scam emails are targeting city employees and residents. Don't click links in unexpected aid emails, and never enter passwords or bank details through one.
body: The City of Corpus Christi is warning employees and residents about phishing emails that impersonate a disaster-aid portal. The emails can look official. They are not.

Phishing emails try to trick you into clicking a link and typing a password, Social Security number or bank information into a fake site. Scammers like to strike after disasters, when people are waiting for help and more likely to click.

"If an email shows up out of nowhere telling you to log in to get your storm aid, stop," said Dwayne Pruitt, the Nueces County emergency management spokesperson, who is passing the city's warning along to county residents. "Don't click. Go to the agency yourself, by typing in an address you know or calling a number you trust."

Red flags: urgent language like "act now" or "your aid will be canceled"; misspelled agency names or logos that look slightly off; web addresses that are close to a real one but not quite; and any request for a password, bank account or Social Security number by email.

If you already clicked: Change your password right away, starting with your email account, and use a different password for every account. If you entered bank information, call your bank. City employees should report suspicious messages to the city's IT staff.

Get aid information from official city, county, state and federal sources, or from local newsrooms you trust, rather than from links in emails or texts you didn't expect. Legitimate agencies will not ask you to send your password by email.
Harborline 6 will update this story with any new guidance from the city. Forward this to someone who's waiting on help.

stories.headline: In Calallen, next door to the water plant, neighbors run their own water routes
stories.summary: Leticia Ramos lives near the O.N. Stevens plant that supplies the whole city. Under a boil-water notice, she has turned her street's group chat into a delivery network.
body: Leticia Ramos keeps a clipboard on the dashboard of her SUV: names, addresses, how many people live in each house, who has a baby, who can't lift a case of water. By Sunday morning the list ran two pages.

Ramos, 45, a schoolteacher, lives in Calallen, a short drive from the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, the only plant that treats water for Corpus Christi. The plant lost both of its power feeds early in Hurricane Rafael on Tuesday, its pumps were damaged, and on Saturday the city issued a citywide boil-water notice.

"We live right next to the plant, and we've got less water than anybody," Ramos said. "I don't need another update that says crews are working diligently. I need to know when, and nobody will tell me when."

On Saturday, Ramos waited in line at a city water distribution site for more than an hour, then made three more trips for neighbors who are elderly, sick or don't have a car. By Sunday she had organized a rotation through her street's group chat: Whoever has gas and a free morning takes the list. The first run left at 7 a.m.

Teresa Gallegos, a spokesperson for the city's water utility, said she understood the frustration. "People who live near the plant see it every day, and they deserve straight answers," Gallegos said. "The straight answer is that we will lift the notice when testing shows the water is safe. Until then, please boil it, and please use the distribution sites."

Health officials say the best protection under the notice is to bring tap water to a rolling boil for two minutes, or use bottled water, for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and mixing baby formula. Hand-washing remains one of the most important things people can do.

The notice covers every tap in the city, from the low-lying neighborhoods near the bay where most 911 calls came from during the storm to the homes around the plant itself. For people without cars, a distribution site across town might as well be across the state, Ramos said. That is who her list is for.
"Teachers know how to run a list," Ramos said, tucking the clipboard back onto the dash before her next run. "This week, this is my class."

stories.headline: A machine counted the damaged houses. What the first Rafael survey can tell us, and what it can't
stories.summary: FEMA's estimate of 4,200 to 5,800 badly damaged structures comes from software reading drone photos. The range is wide for a reason.
body: From a few hundred feet up, a house that lost its roof and a house that kept it are easy to tell apart. A house that kept its roof and took four feet of water is not. That difference sits inside the number FEMA released Saturday, and it is worth understanding before the number hardens into fact.

FEMA Region 6 said between 4,200 and 5,800 structures in Nueces County sustained major or severe damage from Hurricane Rafael. The estimate is based on what the agency called the first systematic aerial drone survey of the Corpus Christi metropolitan area: eight unmanned aircraft, operated under contract by Argus Aerial Systems, covering 180 square kilometers of residential and coastal zones on Friday and Saturday. The count was produced by automated analysis of about 847,000 image tiles.

Start with the range. A gap of 1,600 between the low and high figures is the survey being honest about itself. Software sorts each building into a damage class by what the camera sees: missing roof sections, collapsed walls, debris lines, standing water. Where the picture is ambiguous, the building can fall on either side of a line. FEMA called the figures preliminary and said they will be updated as the survey expands, including to the utility corridor and commercial districts.

Then consider what a camera pointed down cannot see. Surge damage happens low and inside: soaked drywall, ruined wiring, a failed foundation under an intact roof. The neighborhoods that flooded deepest are near the bay and the ship channel, and many of the homes there are older, smaller and rented. If water damage is undercounted anywhere, it is most likely to be undercounted there.

That matters because of how the numbers will be used. FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park said the results are being shared with Nueces County emergency management and the City of Corpus Christi "to inform resource deployment." A map that shows heavy damage draws crews, tarps and inspectors. A map that shows less draws less.

None of this makes the survey wrong. It makes it a first pass. FEMA has said that whether households get direct federal help depends on joint damage assessments, and those involve people walking through homes. For residents, the practical advice is unchanged: photograph the damage inside as well as outside, especially the water line, before cleaning up.

stories.headline: Cuidado con correos falsos que ofrecen ayuda por el desastre / Beware of fake emails offering disaster aid
stories.summary: La ciudad advierte sobre correos que se hacen pasar por un portal de ayuda. Nadie le cobrará por inscribirse. / The city warns of emails impersonating a disaster-aid portal; no one will charge you to sign up.
body: La ciudad de Corpus Christi advirtió a sus empleados y a los residentes sobre correos electrónicos falsos que se hacen pasar por un portal de ayuda por desastre. Los mensajes piden hacer clic en un enlace y escribir datos personales o bancarios.

"Si un correo le pide su contraseña o su número de cuenta para darle ayuda, no es la ayuda. Es una trampa", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, oficial de información pública de la Oficina de Manejo de Emergencias del Condado de Nueces, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. Pruitt pidió escribir usted mismo la dirección de las páginas oficiales en lugar de abrir enlaces.

Recuerde también la advertencia de la oficina del procurador general de Texas y de FEMA: nadie debe cobrarle por inscribirse para recibir ayuda federal, y todavía no hay ninguna inscripción abierta para ayuda a familias. Si alguien le pide dinero para "apartar su lugar", es fraude. Puede reportar fraude a la línea de FEMA para fraude por desastre, 1-866-720-5721.

Si no está seguro de un mensaje, no lo conteste. Llámenos o pregunte en su iglesia o centro comunitario antes de dar cualquier dato. Desconfíe de cualquier mensaje que le exija actuar hoy mismo o que amenace con quitarle la ayuda.

In English: The city of Corpus Christi is warning employees and residents about phishing emails impersonating a disaster-aid portal. "If an email asks for your password or account number to give you help, it's not help. It's a trap," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt. Type official web addresses yourself instead of clicking links. No one should charge you to register for federal aid, and no registration for household aid is open yet; report fraud to FEMA at 1-866-720-5721.

stories.headline: Breathing and skin complaints continue near oiled shorelines; health district urges caution
stories.summary: Health officials say people who live near oiled beaches and marshes should limit time near the water and seek care if symptoms worsen.
body: Residents who live near shorelines oiled by the Inner Harbor spill are still seeking emergency care for breathing problems and skin irritation, health officials and front-line nurses said Sunday, and the health district is urging people to stay away from the oil and limit time near fouled water.

"Crude oil gives off vapors that can irritate the eyes, nose, throat and lungs, and it can irritate skin on contact," said Dr. Anita Shah, an epidemiologist with the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District. "For most people, symptoms ease once they get away from the exposure. People with asthma, COPD or heart disease, older adults, pregnant people and small children should be the most careful."

The Unified Command estimates about 9,000 barrels of crude spilled from two tankers at the Rendal Terminals berth as Hurricane Rafael arrived. Surge and wind carried the oil across about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays and onto North Beach, the Portland shoreline and Nueces Bay marshes. The cause remains under investigation.

In one Nueces County emergency department, charge nurse Alyssa Cortez, 34, said the complaints have been a steady thread all week. "It's not the biggest thing we're seeing, but it's every shift," Cortez said. "People come in coughing, eyes red, and the first thing they tell me is where they live."

Shah said the boil-water notice the city issued Saturday adds a second layer of caution. "We're asking people near the shoreline to stay away from the oil and everyone in the city to boil their water," she said. "Both come down to the same thing: Don't put something in your body that doesn't belong there."

What to do: Keep windows closed and stay inside if fumes are strong. Don't walk, wade or fish in oiled areas; Texas Parks and Wildlife has closed fishing, and the Texas Department of State Health Services has closed shellfish harvesting, in both bays. Wash skin that touches oil with soap and water. Seek care for trouble breathing, chest pain, dizziness or a rash that spreads, and call 911 for severe symptoms.
The health district has not released counts of spill-related visits.

stories.headline: Week ahead: four conditions for a Corpus Christi restart, and none is met yet
stories.summary: A surveyed channel, a contained spill, working utilities and staffed terminals. The first full week after Rafael begins with exports still at zero.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Sabal Energy Wire) — The first full week after Hurricane Rafael begins with crude exports from Corpus Christi still halted and no date for a restart. Analysts say four conditions have to be met first.
A surveyed channel. The Coast Guard has kept the ship channel closed while it is surveyed. Ships that rode out the storm at sea are waiting at the offshore anchorage.

A contained spill. An estimated 9,000 barrels of crude were released from two tankers at the Rendal Terminals berth. Oil has spread into Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. On Saturday the state closed both bays to fishing and shellfish harvesting because of the oil.
Working utilities. The city issued a boil-water notice for all of Corpus Christi on Saturday, and power outages remain widespread. Terminals need power for pumps, lighting and safety systems.

People. Dock workers, line handlers, pilots, tug crews and terminal operators live in the same flooded and powerless neighborhoods as everyone else. A federal major disaster declaration for Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties was approved Saturday.

"Any one of those can hold up the other three," said Grace Holloway, an energy market analyst at Lanternfish Energy Analytics. "The market is used to thinking about the channel. This time the channel is one item on a longer list."

Holloway said she was not attempting a restart forecast. "Anyone who gives you a date is guessing. What I can tell you is the order. Survey first, then the spill, because you cannot move ships through a response. Power and people run in parallel."

She said the fishing closure was a useful indicator for crude traders even though it has nothing to do with tankers. "It tells you the state thinks there is enough oil in that water to matter. The Coast Guard is looking at the same water," she said.
What to watch this week: any Coast Guard statement on the channel survey, the Unified Command's daily updates, and power restoration along the Inner Harbor.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: Opinion: In Rafael's first week, the neighbors got there first
stories.summary: A column. The church halls and street-corner hubs that fed people before official help arrived deserve our thanks, and a hard look at why they had to.
body: The first relief many of my neighbors saw after Hurricane Rafael didn't arrive in a truck with a government seal on the door. It arrived in a borrowed wagon, pulled down a muddy street by a church volunteer.

I've spent this week in the low-lying neighborhoods near the bay, where so many households don't have cars, where people waited for county buses before the storm, and where some stayed home because they had no way to leave. I've watched Pastor Gloria Whitfield turn a fellowship hall into a pantry and a message board. I've watched Rosa Elizondo, a home health aide raising three kids, count water bottles and worry more about her elderly clients than about herself.

Church and neighborhood hubs handed out food and water this week before official distribution reached some of these neighborhoods. That is not a knock on the people working the official response. Many of them haven't slept. Rafael made landfall at 1 a.m. Tuesday with about 11 feet of surge. The 911 center took calls at nearly ten times its normal pace. The city's only water plant lost power, and by Saturday the whole city was under a boil-water notice.

But we should be honest about what it means when help on foot arrives before help on wheels. Advocates warned all summer that transit gaps left households near the bay without a way out. The storm proved them right, and then it proved them right again: The people who couldn't leave were also the people who couldn't drive to help.

So here is what I'd ask. Of the city and county: Find the hubs that opened their doors this week, and send official supplies to them, where people can walk. Of the rest of us: Drop off a case of water at the hall on your way home. Of everyone: Remember this week the next time a hurricane season planning meeting asks who needs a ride, and show up to answer.
Whitfield said this week that nobody asked her church to do this, and nobody needed to. She is right about that. But somebody should have planned so she wouldn't have to.
Marisol Treviño covers city government and disasters for The Bayside Ledger. The views in this column are her own.

stories.headline: Week one after Rafael: Boil your water, watch for scam emails, and depot workers keep standing by
stories.summary: Our weekly roundup for families at NAS Corpus Christi, Corpus Christi Army Depot and NAS Kingsville: what changed this week and what to watch for.
body: It's been a long week. Thank you for checking in, and thank you to every neighbor who checked on someone else. Here's where things stand as of Sunday afternoon.

Boil your water. The city issued a citywide boil-water notice Saturday. Bring tap water to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking, cooking, brushing teeth or mixing formula, or use bottled water. City water distribution sites are open.

Watch your inbox. The City of Corpus Christi has warned its employees and residents about phishing emails dressed up as a disaster-aid portal. Don't click links in unexpected aid emails, and never enter a password or bank information through one. Go to official sites directly. The same caution applies to your work email: If something looks off, report it through your command's normal channels.

Depot workers: Keep standing by. Corpus Christi Army Depot reported hangar roof damage and water intrusion, and workers have been told to stand by until they hear from their supervisors, depot spokesperson Brenda Kowalczyk said Friday.
Bridges are open. The Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway reopened Friday after inspections, so commuters from Portland and Ingleside can cross the bay again.

Stay off oiled shorelines. Oil from the Inner Harbor spill reached North Beach, the Portland shoreline and Nueces Bay marshes. Texas Parks and Wildlife has closed fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services has closed shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, and health officials say to avoid contact with the oil. That includes the fishing spots many of you love along the bay.

About those posts. Station officials said this week that claims the military is seizing homes are false. Some readers have also asked about videos posted online showing lights over the station at night. The station has not commented publicly on them; we will share any statement when there is one.
Aircraft. The training aircraft remain at Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth for now. We'll report return plans as soon as they're announced.
places: NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth

stories.headline: 1,427 survivors: Combined SAR operation stands down after five days; transition to recovery begins
stories.summary: The joint search-and-rescue operation launched after Hurricane Rafael officially stood down Sunday evening with 1,427 confirmed rescues across all agencies, as commanders declare all accessible areas swept and shift to recovery operations.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI — The combined search-and-rescue operation for Hurricane Rafael was formally stood down Sunday evening after five days of continuous operations, with the joint command announcing a confirmed total of 1,427 rescues across all participating agencies — a number that Corpus Christi Fire Chief Alberto Rincón called "an extraordinary testament to the dedication of every person who put a boat in the water or a helicopter in the air in this operation."

Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor and Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi Commander Capt. Delia Ostrowski-Han made the announcement jointly at a late-afternoon press briefing, declaring that all areas accessible by water, ground vehicle, and air asset had been systematically swept and that the operation was transitioning from active search-and-rescue to recovery mode. Under that transition, the focus shifts from locating living survivors to searching for and recovering the remains of those who did not survive, a task that will be managed by law enforcement and medical examiner personnel rather than rescue units.

"We went into every flooded street and every damaged neighborhood that our teams could physically reach," Ostrowski-Han said. "Some streets could not be reached by boat or on foot for the first 48 hours because of surge depth and debris, and there the helicopter crews did the work. Those areas have since been cleared. We are confident that the rescue phase has ended." She noted that the pace had slowed since Thursday evening, when the count stood at 702, and that the last rescues were logged Sunday afternoon.

The 1,427 rescue figure represents a combined count across CCFD swift-water teams, U.S. Coast Guard helicopter and boat crews from Air Station Corpus Christi and Sector Corpus Christi, Nueces County Sheriff's Office marine deputies, Texas Task Force 1 rescue specialists, and multiple mutual aid fire and rescue departments from the surrounding region. Coast Guard and partner helicopter crews accounted for 341 of the rescues, most of them by hoist from rooftops and debris fields, with the remaining evacuations conducted by boat and on foot. The 23 fatalities confirmed as of the stand-down are under investigation by the Nueces County Medical Examiner's office.

stories.headline: Mass rescue ends after five days and 1,427 people; welfare checks begin
stories.summary: County and Coast Guard officials say every known call for rescue has been answered. Residents who have not been contacted by a welfare team should call 211.
body: The boats and helicopters that have worked the flooded neighborhoods of Corpus Christi since Hurricane Rafael made landfall are standing down. Officials said Sunday that mass rescue operations have concluded after five days, with 1,427 confirmed rescues.

The announcement came from Elena Vasquez-Okafor, dispatch chief of the Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center, and Capt. Delia Ostrowski-Han, commander of Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. They said the operation involved 34 coordinated teams at its peak, drawn from the Coast Guard, Texas Task Force 1, the Corpus Christi Fire Department and the Nueces County Sheriff's search and rescue unit.
It also involved 87 civilian boat operators, people with their own boats who were credentialed by the county to work alongside the official teams.

Ostrowski-Han called it the largest helicopter hoist rescue operation in Corpus Christi history. By Wednesday afternoon, the second day of the response, Coast Guard and partner aircraft had already rescued 341 people by air.

Vasquez-Okafor credited the contracted drone operators whose thermal cameras found people in the dark and in debris. "That capability let us put a boat on a specific roof instead of searching a whole block," she said. "It is the difference between minutes and hours."

The end of the rescue phase is not the end of the search. Officials said the remaining teams will shift to welfare checks, going to homes where no one has yet been contacted. Residents who have not been reached by a welfare check team, or who are worried about a neighbor or relative, should call 211.
Search teams recovered two bodies during the operation, both from a submerged vehicle on Violet Road. The county's confirmed storm death toll stands at 23.

The count rose quickly through the week: 486 by Wednesday afternoon, 702 by Thursday evening, 1,427 by Sunday. The steepest climb came after teams moved inland from the bayfront into neighborhoods where the water stayed for days.
The city remains under a boil-water notice issued Saturday, and officials asked residents returning to flooded homes to photograph damage before cleaning up and to stay out of standing water.

stories.headline: Termina el rescate masivo con 1,427 personas a salvo; si nadie ha pasado por su casa, llame al 2-1-1 / Mass rescue ends with 1,427 people saved; if no one has checked on you, call 2-1-1
stories.summary: Los equipos ahora van casa por casa para verificar que la gente esté bien. / Teams are now going door to door on welfare checks.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas — Después de cinco días, las autoridades dieron por terminadas este domingo las operaciones de rescate masivo por el huracán Rafael. En total, 1,427 personas fueron rescatadas, informaron el Centro de Comunicaciones de Emergencia del Coastal Bend y la Guardia Costera.

En el momento de mayor actividad trabajaron 34 equipos coordinados: la Guardia Costera, el equipo Texas Task Force 1, los bomberos de Corpus Christi y la unidad de búsqueda y rescate del alguacil del condado de Nueces. También ayudaron 87 dueños de lanchas particulares, acreditados por el condado. La comandante del sector de la Guardia Costera, la capitana Delia Ostrowski-Han, dijo que fue la operación de rescate con helicóptero más grande en la historia de Corpus Christi.
Que termine el rescate masivo no quiere decir que se acabó la búsqueda. Los equipos que quedan van a pasar casa por casa para verificar que las personas estén bien.

Lo más importante para nuestros oyentes: si ningún equipo ha pasado por su casa, o si usted no ha podido comunicarse con un familiar o un vecino, llame al 2-1-1. La línea atiende en español. Diga la dirección y cuántas personas viven ahí. Si hay una emergencia en este momento, llame al 9-1-1.
Los equipos recuperaron dos cuerpos durante la operación, los dos en un vehículo sumergido en Violet Road. El condado ha confirmado 23 muertes por la tormenta.

Si usted regresa a una casa inundada, tome fotos de los daños antes de limpiar, por dentro y por fuera, y no camine por agua estancada. Recuerde que el aviso de hervir el agua sigue vigente en toda la ciudad: hiérvala durante dos minutos.
En KNCB queremos dar las gracias a los vecinos que salieron con sus propias lanchas.

In English: Officials said Sunday that mass rescue operations have ended after five days, with 1,427 people rescued. Thirty-four teams worked at the peak, along with 87 credentialed civilian boat operators; the Coast Guard called it the largest helicopter hoist rescue operation in Corpus Christi history. Teams are now making door-to-door welfare checks. If no one has checked on your home, or you cannot reach a relative or neighbor, call 2-1-1, which answers in Spanish. The county has confirmed 23 storm deaths. The citywide boil-water notice remains in effect: boil water for two minutes.

stories.headline: Norovirus signal turns up in city wastewater as stomach illness visits rise
stories.summary: Health officials say sewage testing points to norovirus spreading under the citywide boil-water notice. They urge hand-washing with boiled or bottled water and staying home when sick.
body: Wastewater samples from Corpus Christi's treatment plants are showing a norovirus signal, and emergency rooms are seeing a rising number of patients with vomiting and diarrhea, the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District said Monday.

"The sewer tells us what is circulating in the community before most people ever see a doctor," said Dr. Anita Shah, the district epidemiologist who runs its wastewater testing. "Right now it is telling us norovirus is spreading, and the visits we're seeing in the emergency rooms are starting to agree."

Shah did not give a case count. Norovirus, the most common cause of stomach bugs, typically brings on vomiting, diarrhea and cramps a day or two after exposure, and most people recover within a few days.

The signal comes two days after the city issued a citywide boil-water notice. The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant in Calallen, the city's only treatment plant, lost both of its power feeds early in the storm on Sept. 14, and damaged pumps left water pressure low across the system.

Shah said it is too early to say how any single person got sick. Norovirus spreads from person to person, on hands and surfaces, through food and through water. "Families are crowded together, people are standing in lines for water, and a lot of households don't have enough clean water to wash with," she said. "All of that helps it move."
What to do: Boil tap water at a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking it, cooking with it, brushing teeth, making ice or mixing baby formula. Bottled water is safe.

Wash hands with soap and boiled or bottled water, especially after using the bathroom and before eating or cooking. Shah said alcohol-based hand sanitizer does not work well against norovirus and should not replace soap and water.
Clean counters, doorknobs and bathrooms with a bleach solution. Stay home while sick and for two days after symptoms stop, and don't prepare food for others during that time.
Sip water or oral rehydration drinks. Seek care for signs of dehydration, such as very little urine, dizziness or a dry mouth, especially in babies, older adults and people with chronic illness.

stories.headline: Coast Guard examining possible unauthorized remote access to spill tankers' cargo systems
stories.summary: Investigators are looking at the cargo-control systems of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay, the two laden tankers at the center of the Inner Harbor spill. Federal cyber teams are assisting.
body: Investigators are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the cargo-control systems of the two crude tankers involved in the Inner Harbor spill, Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi said Monday. Federal cyber teams are assisting.

MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay were moored laden at the Rendal Terminals berth with Coast Guard approval when Hurricane Rafael came ashore on Mustang Island early Sept. 14. Oil was reported spilling at the berth as the storm arrived. The Unified Command of the Coast Guard and the Texas General Land Office estimates the release at about 9,000 barrels of crude.

"Investigators are examining the possibility of unauthorized remote access to the vessels' cargo-control systems, and federal cyber teams are supporting that work," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a Sector Corpus Christi public affairs officer. "We will not characterize the cause of the discharge until the investigation supports a conclusion."

Until Monday the cause had been described only as under investigation. Ruiz did not say which onboard systems were being examined, what type of access was involved or whether any other vessels were affected.

Cargo-control systems on modern tankers monitor and manage cargo handling, including tank levels and pumps during loading and discharge. Many operators allow approved technicians to connect to those systems from shore for maintenance and software support.

Rendal Terminals, which operates the berth, said it is cooperating. "Rendal Terminals is cooperating fully with the Unified Command and with federal investigators," spokesman Victor Lang said. "We will not comment on the substance of an active investigation."

Port conditions: The port has been closed to inbound traffic since Sept. 12, when crude exports halted, and the ship channel to all traffic since Sept. 13. Vessels that put to sea for the storm are back at the offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas. The Coast Guard has not announced a reopening date. The Unified Command requested Navy salvage equipment early in the response, and crews began deploying boom once winds dropped.
places: Crude terminal on the Inner Harbor ship channel
US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi
Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: Detectan señal de norovirus en las aguas residuales; aumentan las visitas por malestar estomacal / Norovirus signal found in wastewater; stomach illness visits rising
stories.summary: El distrito de salud pide lavarse las manos con jabón y seguir hirviendo el agua. Cuándo llevar a un niño o a un adulto mayor al médico. / Health officials urge handwashing and continued boiling. When to seek care.
body: Las pruebas de las aguas residuales de Corpus Christi muestran una señal de norovirus, y las visitas a las clínicas y salas de emergencia por malestar estomacal están aumentando, informó hoy el distrito de salud pública.

El norovirus causa vómito y diarrea y se contagia con mucha facilidad de persona a persona, por las manos y por las superficies. Después de una tormenta, con familias compartiendo casa, baños y comida, se propaga más rápido.

"Las aguas residuales nos avisan antes que las salas de emergencia, y lo que vemos es una señal clara", dijo la doctora Anita Shah, epidemióloga del distrito de salud, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Lávense las manos con agua y jabón. El gel antibacterial solo no basta contra este virus. Y sigan hirviendo el agua."

El aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente en toda la ciudad. Hierva el agua a borbotones durante dos minutos antes de beberla, cocinar o lavarse los dientes. Para lavarse las manos, use agua hervida o embotellada si puede.
Si alguien en casa se enferma:
Dele líquidos poco a poco: suero oral, agua hervida ya fría, caldos.
Que no prepare comida para los demás mientras tenga síntomas y hasta dos días después.
Limpie el baño y las superficies con cloro diluido.
Busque atención médica si un niño pequeño o un adulto mayor no puede retener líquidos, si hay sangre en las heces, fiebre alta o señales de deshidratación como boca seca y poca orina.
Los hospitales siguen muy ocupados por la tormenta. Si no es una emergencia, llame primero a su clínica.

In English: Wastewater testing in Corpus Christi shows a norovirus signal, and visits for stomach illness are rising, the health district said. "Wash your hands with soap and water. Hand sanitizer alone isn't enough for this virus. And keep boiling your water," said epidemiologist Dr. Anita Shah. The citywide boil-water notice remains in effect: boil water for two minutes. Seek care if a young child or older adult cannot keep fluids down or shows signs of dehydration.

stories.headline: Investigators examine possible remote access to tankers in Texas hurricane oil spill
stories.summary: The Coast Guard says federal cyber teams are helping examine the cargo-control systems of two tankers that released about 9,000 barrels of crude as Hurricane Rafael closed in on Corpus Christi.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Federal investigators are examining whether someone gained unauthorized remote access to the cargo-control systems of two crude tankers that spilled oil into Corpus Christi's harbor as Hurricane Rafael arrived last week, the Coast Guard said Monday.

Rafael came ashore on Mustang Island near Port Aransas around 1 a.m. on Sept. 14 as a Category 3 hurricane, pushing about 11 feet of surge into Corpus Christi and Nueces bays. As the storm arrived, oil began spilling from the MT Kalvora Star and the MT Ostrel Bay, two laden tankers moored at an Inner Harbor terminal. The Coast Guard and the Texas General Land Office, which lead a Unified Command on the spill, put the release at about 9,000 barrels.

The surge and wind then carried the oil out of the ship channel. Sheen has covered about 33 square miles of the two bays, and oil has reached shorelines on North Beach and in Portland as well as coastal marshes.

Investigators are looking into possible unauthorized remote access to the vessels' cargo-control systems, with federal cyber teams helping, said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a spokeswoman for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. "We are not going to get ahead of the investigation," she said.

Kim Tran, a regional cybersecurity advisor with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said the agency is supporting the Coast Guard. "Our job right now is to help investigators and the companies involved understand whether and how those systems were reached," Tran said. "It is too early to talk about findings."
Officials did not say who, if anyone, may have accessed the systems, or when.

The stakes reach beyond the Texas coast. The Port of Corpus Christi handles about half of the nation's crude oil exports, by analysts' estimates, and those exports have been halted since the Coast Guard closed the port to inbound traffic on Sept. 12, two days before landfall.

The spill is one of several crises still unfolding along the Coastal Bend nearly a week after the storm, as residents contend with flooded homes, a damaged water system and a citywide order to boil tap water.
places: Crude terminal on the Inner Harbor ship channel

stories.headline: Coast Guard completes inspections aboard Kalvora Star and Ostrel Bay; both tankers held at berth
stories.summary: Marine inspectors and pollution investigators finished aboard both ships Sunday. Crews are safe, and neither vessel moves until the investigation and the owners' spill obligations are addressed.
body: Coast Guard marine inspectors and pollution investigators completed inspections Sunday aboard MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay, the two laden tankers at the Rendal Terminals berth from which an estimated 9,000 barrels of crude were released as Hurricane Rafael arrived, Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi said Monday.
Crews. Both crews are safe, the sector said.

Vessel status. Both tankers remain moored at the berth under a Captain of the Port order. Neither will move until the investigation and the owners' obligations under federal oil spill law are addressed. The sector gave no timeline.

Scope. Investigators documented the condition of the cargo systems on both ships. The statement repeats what the Coast Guard disclosed earlier Monday: investigators are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems, with federal cyber teams assisting. The Coast Guard said it will not characterize the cause of the release while the investigation is open.
"The inspections are complete, the vessels are staying where they are, and the cause is not something I can discuss," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, the sector's public affairs officer.
Rendal Terminals said it is cooperating. "We are cooperating fully with the Unified Command and with investigators," said Victor Lang, a company spokesperson.
Response. Containment boom is deployed along affected shoreline in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. Fishing and shellfish harvesting in both bays have been closed since Saturday.

Operator notes. Two loaded tankers held at an Inner Harbor berth, with a safety zone around them, are now fixed features of any reopening plan. Deep-draft traffic to berths farther up the Inner Harbor has to pass them. The Coast Guard has not said how it will sequence that, and the channel remains closed to all traffic. The formal responsible-party designation the Unified Command said to expect has not yet been issued.

stories.headline: Training aircraft begin returning to NAS Corpus Christi and NAS Kingsville
stories.summary: Aircraft that rode out Rafael at NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth are coming home. Station officials also say they are aware of residents' reports of drones and are working with authorities.
body: Training aircraft that flew north ahead of Hurricane Rafael began returning to NAS Corpus Christi and NAS Kingsville on Monday, station officials said, a sight many families had been waiting for since the planes left for NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth before the storm.

"Seeing our aircraft back on the ramp is a big step for the whole team," said Lt. Marcus Hale, NAS Corpus Christi public affairs officer. "Our people have worked hard to get the airfield ready, and we're grateful to our hosts in Fort Worth for keeping the aircraft safe."
As always, Anchor & Rotor does not report aircraft numbers or flight schedules. Squadron members should follow their chain of command for duty and reporting guidance.

Hale also addressed the videos many of you have seen on social media since last week showing lights hovering over the air station at night. "NAS Corpus Christi is aware of the reports of drones and is working with the appropriate authorities," he said. "There is no impact to operations." He declined to discuss security measures, which the station does not comment on.

At Corpus Christi Army Depot, crews are still dealing with the hangar roof damage and water intrusion the depot reported Friday. Depot employees were told to stand by and should watch for word from their supervisors on returning to work.

For families: Off-base households in Corpus Christi remain under the city's boil-water notice issued Saturday. Boil tap water at a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking, cooking, brushing teeth or mixing formula, or use bottled water.

Health officials also reported Monday that wastewater testing shows norovirus and that stomach illness visits are rising. Wash hands with soap and boiled or bottled water, keep sick children home, and check in on neighbors who may not have water or transportation.
If you need help, your command's family readiness contacts are the first stop. We'll keep updating as the station shares more.
places: NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth

stories.headline: Flour Bluff stargazer's videos of lights over the air station draw questions
stories.summary: Jaime Ortega has filmed lights hovering over NAS Corpus Christi on several nights since Rafael. He says he doesn't know what they are. The Navy says it is working with authorities.
body: FLOUR BLUFF — Jaime Ortega sets up his tripod in the backyard most clear nights. Since Hurricane Rafael, his camera keeps catching something he can't explain.

Ortega, 42, is a hobby astronomer. He has filmed lights hovering over NAS Corpus Christi on several nights since the storm, and his first video went up last week. Clips from Ortega and other residents are now spreading across local social media.

"I know what planes look like. I know what satellites look like," Ortega tells Harborline 6. "These hold still for a long time, then they move off. I can't tell you what they are. I can tell you I filmed them, and I'd like somebody to tell us."
Harborline 6 reviewed several of his clips. They show small points of light over the base, some steady and some blinking, against a dark sky.

NAS Corpus Christi says it knows about the reports. "NAS Corpus Christi is aware of the reports of drones and is working with the appropriate authorities," public affairs officer Lt. Marcus Hale said Monday. "There is no impact to operations." The Navy is not discussing security measures.

Ortega says he is careful about what he posts. He keeps his camera's time stamps on and does not guess. "The internet will tell you it's aliens or some big conspiracy," he says. "It's lights. That's what I've got."

What to do if you see something: Note the time, direction and how long it lasts. Don't fly your own drone near the base; federal rules restrict drone flights near many military installations. Do not go onto base property. Report what you see to police.

stories.headline: In Calallen, a schoolteacher runs the water line for her street
stories.summary: A week after Rafael, Leticia Ramos keeps a clipboard of which neighbors need water and who has a car. Her street sits a few minutes from the plant whose failure led to the citywide boil-water notice.
body: By Leticia Ramos' front door hangs a clipboard, and on it is her whole street: house numbers, household sizes, who drives, who has a newborn, who needs help lifting.

Ramos, 45, a schoolteacher, lives a few minutes from the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant in Calallen. Since Hurricane Rafael knocked out the plant's power a week ago, she has organized her street's water runs, matching neighbors who have cars with neighbors who don't and keeping track of who needs what.

"I teach, so I make lists," she said Tuesday, loading jugs into a garden wagon. "The older couple two doors down can't stand in a line in this heat. The family on the corner has a newborn. Somebody has to keep track, and I'm home."

The plant, the city's only water treatment plant, lost both of its power feeds early in the storm on Sept. 14. Pumps were damaged, and water pressure dropped across the city. On Saturday the city issued a citywide boil-water notice and opened water distribution sites.

Ramos said what wears on her street is not the boiling but the waiting. "We hear 'soon' and 'working on it,'" she said. "Tell us what's broken and when it'll be fixed. People can handle the truth. They can't plan around 'soon.'"

The frustration is understandable, said Teresa Gallegos, a spokeswoman for the city's water utility. "We know how hard this is, and we're sorry," Gallegos said. "Crews are working on the plant around the clock. Until we tell you otherwise, boil your water. We will give people a timeline when we have one we can stand behind."

The stakes went up Monday, when the city-county health district said wastewater testing shows a norovirus signal and stomach illness visits are rising. Ramos has added a new item to her runs: a jug of boiled water and a bar of soap by every front door that needs one.
"Hand-washing, that's the lesson this week," she said. "I'd rather teach fractions."
By late afternoon the wagon was empty again. She checked off two more houses and went inside to boil another pot.

stories.headline: Coast Guard files formal SAR incident report: 1,427 rescues, 341 by helicopter, operation complete
stories.summary: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi has filed Incident Summary Report ISR-2027-CC-004 formally closing the Hurricane Rafael search-and-rescue operation with 1,427 confirmed rescues, 341 of them by helicopter.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI — The U.S. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi filed Incident Summary Report ISR-2027-CC-004 on Tuesday, formally archiving the Hurricane Rafael search-and-rescue operation and certifying its final statistics: 1,427 confirmed rescues — 341 by helicopter hoist, 1,041 by surface vessel and 45 ambulatory survivor contacts — over an operational period from the first launch at 1:22 a.m. on September 14 through stand-down on September 19.

The ISR, a formal Coast Guard record required for all major SAR incidents, was submitted to Coast Guard District 8 and will serve as the authoritative source document for the operational record of the rescue phase of the Rafael response. Sector Corpus Christi Commander Capt. Delia Ostrowski-Han signed the report as the cognizant Coast Guard authority. "This document is not a celebration," Ostrowski-Han said at a Tuesday morning briefing. "It is a record of an extraordinary effort under the worst conditions this community has faced in decades. The numbers represent real people whose lives were saved by the men and women of the Coast Guard, the fire department, the sheriff's office, and Task Force 1."

The ISR documents the operational sequencing of the rescue effort, from the initial activation of Air Station Corpus Christi's alert crews before Rafael's landfall through the final grid sweeps of south Mustang Island on the fifth day of operations. It notes the critical role of thermal imaging from the HH-60 Jayhawks in locating survivors during the nighttime hours immediately following landfall, when ground-based rescue units were unable to safely enter the surge zone. The document also acknowledges the unprecedented call volume handled by the Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center — about 2,900 calls in a single day — as a key factor in the coordination of multi-agency rescue assets.

The report will be submitted to the Coast Guard's Rescue 21 SAR database and to the Interagency Committee on Search and Rescue for statistical archiving. Anchor and Rotor Weekly has obtained a summary of the ISR through a Coast Guard public affairs request. The 23 confirmed fatalities remain under investigation by the Nueces County Medical Examiner, with final cause-of-death determinations expected within 60 to 90 days. The Coast Guard will conduct a formal lessons-learned debrief with its SAR partners in the coming months.

stories.headline: Coast Guard files Rafael SAR summary: 341 hoists, 1,041 surface rescues; after-action review due in 90 days
stories.summary: Sector Corpus Christi's incident summary report certifies 1,427 rescues and credits contracted drone operators with 112 thermal annotations used by surface craft.
body: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi has filed its formal Incident Summary Report for the Hurricane Rafael search and rescue operation with Coast Guard District 8, the sector said Tuesday. The report, ISR-2027-CC-004, certifies 1,427 total rescues.

Breakdown as certified: 341 by helicopter hoist; 1,041 by surface vessel, a category that covers Coast Guard, state and civilian craft; and 45 ambulatory survivor contacts, meaning people who were found and assisted but did not need to be lifted or carried out.

The surface figure is the one of interest to the working waterfront. Nearly three of every four rescues were made from the water, in flooded streets and along the bay shore, not from the air. County officials said Sunday that 87 credentialed civilian boat operators worked alongside the official teams, and that 34 teams were coordinated at the peak of the operation.

The report also notes that contracted unmanned aircraft operators provided 112 thermal imaging annotations that were used directly to coordinate surface rescues. In practice that means a marked position passed from an aircraft to a boat crew.

Timeline from Coast Guard and county statements: helicopter operations began at 1:22 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 14. By 3 p.m. Wednesday, Sept. 15, crews had completed 180 hoists and all rescues by air stood at 341, with 486 people reached in total. The cumulative count was 702 on Thursday evening and 1,427 when mass rescue operations concluded Sunday, Sept. 19.

Channel status is unchanged. The Corpus Christi Ship Channel has been closed to all traffic since Port Condition Zulu was set at noon on Monday, Sept. 13, and remains closed for damage surveys and for the oil spill response in the Inner Harbor. Rescue craft operated inside the bays under Coast Guard direction; no commercial movements have resumed.

A formal after-action review of the SAR operation will be conducted within 90 days, the Coast Guard said. For operators, the items to watch in that review are how civilian vessels were credentialed and tasked, how positions were passed between aircraft, drones and boats, and whether those arrangements are written into the area's contingency plans before next season.
The Coast Guard thanked the community and its mutual-aid partners for their response.
places: US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi

stories.headline: A week after the spill, North Beach lives with the smell, and some with the cough
stories.summary: Oil carried by Rafael's surge still marks shorelines and marshes. Health officials say residents near oiled areas should avoid contact with it and get care for breathing or skin problems.
body: The first thing Marcus Bell notices when he steps outside his North Beach house in the morning is the smell. It is fainter than it was in the first days after the storm, he says, but it is still there, sharp and oily, when the wind comes off the water.
"I welded my whole working life around fuel and fumes," said Bell, 67. "I know that smell. You don't forget it."

A week ago, Hurricane Rafael's surge and wind carried oil out of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel and into Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. Sheen spread across about 33 square miles of water, and oil came ashore on North Beach, on Portland's shoreline and in marshes along the bays. The Unified Command has estimated that about 9,000 barrels of crude were released from two tankers, MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay, at the Rendal Terminals berth on the Inner Harbor.

For North Beach, the spill landed on top of everything else. When the Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway closed as Rafael hit, residents like Bell were cut off from downtown until inspections finished and the bridges reopened Friday.
Since then, emergency rooms have seen respiratory and skin complaints from people living near oiled shorelines, according to the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District.

"If you live near the shoreline and you have a cough, a scratchy throat, headaches or a rash, you are not imagining it, and you should get checked," said Dr. Anita Shah, a district epidemiologist. "Most of those symptoms ease once people avoid exposure. The most important thing is to stay out of the oil and keep children and pets away from it."
Shah said residents who get oil on their skin should wash it off with soap and water, not solvents, and should not try to clean up oiled areas themselves.
Bell has mostly stayed inside with the windows shut. "My throat's been raw for days," he said. "I'm not going to the beach. Nobody's going to the beach."

Cleanup crews began deploying boom once winds dropped, and the state has opened a wildlife hotline for oiled birds and animals. Texas Parks and Wildlife and the Texas Department of State Health Services have closed fishing and shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.
For Bell, the questions are simpler. "When does it go away," he said, "and who pays for my neighbors' doctor bills?"
places: Crude terminal on the Inner Harbor ship channel
US 181 Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway

stories.headline: Most of Rafael's rescues came by boat. Many of the boats belonged to the neighbors
stories.summary: The Coast Guard's final count credits surface craft with 1,041 of 1,427 rescues. Eighty-seven of the people at the helm were civilians.
body: The pictures people will remember from Hurricane Rafael are of helicopters: an orange-and-white Jayhawk holding steady over a roof in Flour Bluff, a rescue swimmer going down the wire. The numbers the Coast Guard filed Tuesday tell a somewhat different story. Most of the people who were rescued left by boat.

Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi said it has submitted its formal summary of the search and rescue operation to Coast Guard District 8. The report certifies 1,427 rescues: 341 by helicopter hoist, 1,041 by surface vessel and 45 ambulatory survivor contacts. The surface count includes Coast Guard, state and civilian craft.

The civilians were not an afterthought. When officials announced the end of mass rescue operations on Sunday, they said 87 credentialed civilian boat operators had worked alongside 34 coordinated teams from the Coast Guard, Texas Task Force 1, the Corpus Christi Fire Department and the Nueces County Sheriff's search and rescue unit.

Credentialed is the important word. In the military and in the Coast Guard, an operation works because everyone in it is known to whoever is running it: who they are, what they are driving, where they have been sent. A volunteer in a bay boat becomes useful to a rescue the moment a dispatcher can give that boat an address and hear back what was found. Without that, the boat is one more thing in the water to keep track of.

The same idea shows up in a line of the report about drones.
