The joint program is limited to detection: it can locate a drone and its operator but cannot bring an aircraft down. The agencies said the network will be operated in coordination with the FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations.

The disclosure that drone activity was retroactively identified above critical infrastructure in the pre-storm period is significant in the context of the confirmed cyberattack on CBPWA's industrial control systems and the broader federal investigation. Law enforcement officials have not publicly discussed the drone activity or its potential relationship to the cyberattack; the FBI declined to comment Saturday. Aviation security specialists noted that pre-attack drone reconnaissance of industrial facilities has been documented in other infrastructure incident investigations.

Port spokesperson Javier Salinas and CBPWA did not answer specific questions about the drone findings at Saturday's briefing. "Our focus is on protecting the facilities going forward," Salinas said. "We identified a gap. We are closing it." The FAA's temporary flight restriction over the area in September was the hurricane restriction and is unrelated to the new program.

stories.headline: Federal investigators refer 847 social media accounts for removal after Rafael disinformation campaign traced to coordinated network
stories.summary: Texas TDEM and federal partners have identified 847 accounts across multiple platforms that amplified false shelter locations as the storm approached, later pivoted to blaming ERCOT for prolonged outages, and are now promoting what investigators characterize as a "coverup" narrative about the utility cyberattack.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Texas Division of Emergency Management and federal partners have identified 847 social media accounts engaged in what investigators describe as a coordinated information operation targeting Hurricane Rafael response and recovery, and have referred them to major platforms for removal. CISA published an advisory Saturday characterizing the activity as a coordinated influence behavior campaign that exploited the storm's emergency information environment across three distinct phases.

According to the CISA advisory, the accounts amplified false emergency shelter locations in the five days before Rafael's landfall. Separately, 23 false emergency calls made to Corpus Christi's 911 center a week after landfall have been referred to the FBI. In a second phase, the same network promoted a narrative attributing the extended power outages in Corpus Christi's bay neighborhoods to failures by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, the state's power grid operator, rather than to hurricane damage. ERCOT has no operational role in CBPWA's distribution system.

Following the Oct. 5 public disclosure of the utility cyberattack, the accounts shifted again, now promoting what CISA characterized as a "this is a coverup" narrative — claiming that federal investigators are concealing information about the attack's perpetrators or scope. The advisory warns that the coverup narrative is "designed to undermine public confidence in the ongoing federal investigation and in official communications from the utility and emergency management agencies."

"Texas TDEM and federal partners have identified and referred 847 social media accounts to platforms for removal," the CISA advisory states. "These accounts amplified false shelter locations, promoted an ERCOT-blame narrative, and are now promoting a coverup theory regarding the utility cyberattack. The coordinated nature of the account activity is consistent with an influence operation rather than organic public concern." CISA did not attribute the operation to any specific actor or state in the advisory; that assessment, if made, has not been made public.

Platform companies have not confirmed they received or acted on the referrals as of Saturday. Media researchers who study coordinated inauthentic behavior said the three-phase structure described in the advisory is consistent with operations designed to cause sustained disruption across the full arc of a disaster response. "Phase one is operational disruption during the emergency itself. Phase two is political attribution to maximize blame. Phase three is epistemic — you undermine the public's ability to trust any official account," said one disinformation researcher who reviewed the advisory. "If this characterization is accurate, it's a relatively sophisticated playbook."

stories.headline: Relief ship Gulf Provider finally docks with 40 containers
stories.summary: The cargo ship waited weeks in the offshore backlog. Its relief containers are coming off at the Port of Corpus Christi this morning.
body: MV Gulf Provider is alongside. After weeks in the offshore anchorage line, the relief cargo ship is at a berth at the Port of Corpus Christi this morning. Its 40 relief containers are coming off.
Cranes swing. Trucks idle in a line along the dock road. A worker in a hard hat waves them forward, one at a time.

The containers were booked five days before Hurricane Rafael made landfall. Then the Coast Guard closed the ship channel ahead of the storm, and the ship ended up in the queue offshore. For a cargo ship, that is a long time to sit within sight of the coast. The channel partly reopened Thursday, but the anchorage backlog kept Gulf Provider waiting until now.

"It's about a month later than anybody wanted," says Javier Salinas, spokesperson for the Port of Corpus Christi. "But it's here, it's moving, and the channel is doing what it's supposed to do. We're glad to see these boxes on the dock."
What's inside? The port describes the cargo as relief supplies. Harborline 6 is asking relief agencies where it will be distributed and will update this story.
The wait was part of a bigger backlog. Two days before landfall, when the port closed to inbound traffic, 14 vessels were left holding at the offshore anchorage, and crude exports stopped with them.
Waiting on help? Check with your neighborhood hub or relief agency for updated distribution hours this week.
The inner ship channel is still restricted for spill decontamination. The citywide boil-water notice remains in effect.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: Llega al muelle el Gulf Provider con 40 contenedores de ayuda, con un mes de retraso / Gulf Provider berths with 40 relief containers, about a month late
stories.summary: La carga se reservó antes de la tormenta y esperó semanas frente a la costa mientras el canal estuvo cerrado. / The cargo was booked before the storm and waited offshore for weeks while the channel was closed.
body: El buque de carga MV Gulf Provider atracó hoy en el Puerto de Corpus Christi y descargó 40 contenedores de ayuda humanitaria, alrededor de un mes más tarde de lo planeado.

La carga se había reservado antes de que Rafael tocara tierra, cuando el cono del pronóstico apenas alcanzaba a Corpus Christi. Después vinieron el cierre del canal, el derrame de petróleo y, desde el jueves, una reapertura parcial con una larga fila de barcos esperando turno en el fondeadero frente a la costa.

"Esos contenedores se reservaron para llegar justo después de la tormenta", dijo Terry Akins, gerente regional de Gulf Relief Logistics, la empresa que organizó el envío, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "En lugar de eso pasaron semanas en el fondeadero. Hoy por fin están en tierra. Ojalá hubiera sido hace un mes."

En el salón de su iglesia, la pastora Gloria Whitfield recibió la noticia con su franqueza de siempre. "Más vale tarde que nunca, pero tarde es tarde", dijo. "En este barrio la primera ayuda la pusieron los mismos vecinos."
El salón, que reparte comida y agua desde los primeros días después de la tormenta, mantiene el horario que tiene pegado en la puerta.
Qué sigue: las organizaciones de ayuda repartirán la carga a través de sus propias bodegas y puntos de distribución. KNCB preguntó cuándo y dónde, y leerá al aire los horarios en cuanto los tenga.
Si usted necesita comida, agua o artículos de limpieza hoy, llame al 2-1-1 y pida información en español sobre el punto de distribución más cercano.
Recordatorio: el aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente en la ciudad.

In English: The cargo ship MV Gulf Provider berthed at the Port of Corpus Christi on Sunday and unloaded 40 relief containers, about a month late. The cargo was booked before landfall and waited at the offshore anchorage through the channel closure and partial reopening. "Today they're finally ashore. I wish it had been a month ago," said Terry Akins of Gulf Relief Logistics. "Better late than never, but late is late," said Pastor Gloria Whitfield, whose church hall has handed out food and water since the first days after the storm.

stories.headline: A month late, Gulf Provider's 40 relief containers come ashore
stories.summary: The relief cargo booked before Hurricane Rafael spent weeks in the anchorage backlog. The freight forwarder says the delay shows how much a single closed channel can hold up.
body: The 40 relief containers aboard MV Gulf Provider were booked five days before Hurricane Rafael made landfall. On Sunday, about a month late, they came ashore at the Port of Corpus Christi.

The cargo ship berthed and began unloading after weeks in the backlog at the offshore anchorage, where ships have waited since returning from sea after the storm. The channel partly reopened Thursday, as the Ledger reported, but spill decontamination still restricts the inner channel and ships are moving in sequence.

"Forty boxes, one month, one channel," said Terry Akins, regional manager for Gulf Relief Logistics, the freight forwarder handling the shipment. "That's the whole supply chain lesson right there. You can have the cargo, the ship, the trucks and the customer, and if the channel's shut, you've got a very expensive parking lot offshore."

Akins said the containers would be released to relief agencies as they clear the dock. He would not estimate when all 40 would reach their destinations, saying that depends on trucking and on how quickly receiving sites can take deliveries.

Javier Salinas, a spokesperson for the Port of Corpus Christi, said the berthing showed the partial reopening was doing its job. "Every day we move more of the queue," he said. "We know how much this particular cargo matters to people here."

The numbers behind the delay are stark. At closure, 14 vessels were waiting offshore. The port, which handles about half of U.S. crude exports, spent the month after landfall with no way in or out for the ships that keep it running, until Thursday's partial reopening.
For relief shippers, Akins said, the lesson is to treat the channel as a single point of failure. "I had one lane, and the lane closed," he said. "That's on me to fix before next season."
Gulf Provider's cargo arrives as residents across the city are still boiling water under the citywide notice issued four days after landfall.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: MV Gulf Provider berths and lands 40 relief containers, about a month late
stories.summary: The cargo was booked before Rafael and waited offshore through the closure and the backlog that followed the partial reopening. Inner-channel restrictions remain.
body: MV Gulf Provider berthed at Corpus Christi on Sunday and unloaded 40 relief containers, about a month after the cargo was meant to arrive.

The containers were booked before Hurricane Rafael by the freight forwarder Gulf Relief Logistics. The ship waited at the offshore anchorage through the storm closure, then waited again in the backlog that built when the channel partly reopened Thursday.

"Those boxes were booked five days before landfall. They touched the dock today," said Terry Akins, the company's regional manager. "Nobody on that ship did anything wrong. Nobody at the port did anything wrong. We had a plan that depended on one channel, and the channel was shut."
Port condition. Partly open. Spill decontamination continues to restrict the inner channel, which limits how many ships can work the Inner Harbor berths and slows the turn of those that do.

Why relief cargo waited after the reopening. A partial reopening does not clear an anchorage. Transits resumed under conditions, and the line offshore held weeks of arrivals. Sequencing put ships through by draft, berth and readiness as well as priority.

"Getting that ship alongside was a priority for us within the limits we are working under," said Javier Salinas, a spokesman for the Port of Corpus Christi. "The backlog is real and it is shrinking. Every day the channel stays open, the line gets shorter."

What was aboard. Akins described the cargo as general relief supplies consigned to agencies working in the three coastal counties. Trucks began moving containers off the terminal the same afternoon, he said.

Operator notes. Expect the backlog at the anchorage to persist while the inner channel stays restricted. Confirm decontamination requirements with the Coast Guard and the terminal before arrival. Ships bound for berths outside the restricted reach should say so early; it affects their place in the line.
Gulfwater first reported on the forwarder's standby contracts in August.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: Relief airlift begins at NAS Corpus Christi: what families should know
stories.summary: Forty relief flights, military C-17s and civilian charters, are due at the air station over the next ten days. Expect bigger aircraft and more noise.
body: If the windows rattle a little more than usual this week, here's why: relief flights have started landing at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi.

Over the next ten days, 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charter flights are scheduled to bring relief supplies into the station, according to NAS Corpus Christi public affairs. For a base whose skies usually belong to training aircraft, that is a lot of very large airplanes.

"The air station is proud to support the relief effort for our neighbors across the Coastal Bend," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for NAS Corpus Christi. "Families may notice larger aircraft and more activity around the airfield. We'll put out notices through official channels if anything changes for base services."

The airlift caps a long month for the station. Training aircraft flew to NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth ahead of Hurricane Rafael and began returning six days after landfall. Corpus Christi Army Depot, which sits on the station, reported hangar roof damage and water intrusion from the storm and told workers to stand by.

The flights also begin a day after the cargo ship MV Gulf Provider unloaded 40 relief containers at the Port of Corpus Christi, about a month late, after waiting in the anchorage backlog. Help is now arriving by sea and by air.

A few reminders for families this week. Expect daytime aircraft noise, and plan naps and nervous pets accordingly. Get base news from official station channels, not from screenshots. And if you see a post that seems designed to make you angry or afraid, check it before you share it; false rumors and lookalike aid sites have circulated widely since the storm.
Thank you, as always, for being good neighbors. Anchor & Rotor will keep track of the airlift through the week.
places: NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth

stories.headline: Forty flights in ten days: how the relief airlift into NAS Corpus Christi works
stories.summary: Military C-17s and civilian charters are landing at a base best known for training Navy pilots. Here's why the air station, and why now.
body: Naval Air Station Corpus Christi is a training base. On an ordinary weekday, the sky over Flour Bluff belongs to turboprop trainers flown by student aviators. Starting Monday, it also belongs to C-17s.

Over the next ten days, 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charter flights are scheduled to land at the station with relief supplies, according to NAS Corpus Christi. The airlift is a visible new phase in the Coastal Bend's recovery from Hurricane Rafael, which made landfall on Mustang Island on Sept. 14.

Why an air station? A military airfield offers long runways, room to park and unload large cargo aircraft, and a secure place to stage freight before it moves on by truck. The C-17, the Air Force's workhorse cargo jet, can carry outsized loads into shorter runways than most airliners need, which is why it shows up after disasters.

"Our job is to give the relief effort a safe place to land and unload," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the station. "The cargo belongs to the agencies doing the work in the community. We're the front porch."

Why now? The airlift comes as the region's sea route is only partly back. The Coast Guard partly reopened the Corpus Christi Ship Channel last Thursday, with the inner channel still restricted for spill decontamination and ships queued at the offshore anchorage. On Sunday, the relief cargo ship MV Gulf Provider unloaded 40 containers, about a month after they were booked. Air and sea are now working the same problem from two directions.

The civilian charters operate under different rules than military aircraft, but Hale said all flights follow the same airfield procedures once they arrive. The station did not release daily flight schedules, which is standard practice at military airfields, and this story does not include them.

The airlift also marks another step back toward routine for the station itself. Its training aircraft flew to NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth before the storm and began returning six days after landfall. For neighbors in Flour Bluff, the difference this week is in the sound: lower, heavier, and a lot more of it.
places: NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth

stories.headline: With ER hallways clear again, health officials say keep boiling until the notice lifts
stories.summary: ER visits for stomach illness are well down from their peak after Hurricane Rafael, and complaints near oiled shorelines are easing. The boil-water notice remains in effect.
body: The worst of the stomach illness that crowded Corpus Christi emergency rooms after Hurricane Rafael has passed, health officials say. Their advice has not changed: keep boiling your water until the city says otherwise.

Wastewater testing picked up a norovirus signal in the days after the city issued its boil-water notice on Sept. 18, and ER visits for stomach illness climbed to about 180% above normal, with hallway beds in use. Those visits began to ease about two weeks after landfall.

"The trend is good, and it's good because people have been careful," said Dr. Anita Shah, an epidemiologist with the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District. "Norovirus spreads easily. It only takes one lapse, a glass straight from the tap or ice from the freezer tray, to start it again in a household. Boil your water, wash your hands with soap, and clean surfaces if someone at home is sick."

Alyssa Cortez, 34, a charge nurse in a Nueces County emergency department, said the change shows at the triage desk. "A few weeks ago I had people in hallway beds holding buckets," she said. "Now the hallway is a hallway again. I'd like to keep it that way. So please, boil the water."
Complaints of breathing trouble and skin irritation among residents near oiled shorelines are also easing, health officials said earlier this month. Their guidance remains to avoid contact with oil.

What to do: Bring tap water to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking it, cooking with it, brushing teeth or making ice. Use boiled or bottled water for baby formula. If someone in your home has vomiting or diarrhea, keep them home until at least two days after symptoms stop, and seek care for signs of dehydration, such as dizziness or very little urine.

The notice will stay in place until repairs at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant are complete and testing confirms the water is safe, the utility has said. Replacement pump parts were delayed after the supplier's local warehouse flooded.

stories.headline: Port and utility to field drone-detection network across infrastructure corridor
stories.summary: The joint initiative follows a federal report on unauthorized drone flights before Rafael. The sensing network is expected to be working within 90 days.
body: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority will deploy a drone-detection network across the port and utility corridor, the two agencies announced Saturday.

What it is. A radio-frequency sensing and direction-finding network at multiple sites, operated in coordination with the Federal Aviation Administration and Customs and Border Protection's Air and Marine Operations. The agencies said Sentinel Airspace Inc. was selected as the technology provider after a competitive evaluation.
When. The network is expected to be operational within 90 days.

Why. The announcement cites a recommendation in the joint FAA and CBP report on unauthorized drone activity before Hurricane Rafael. The two federal agencies confirmed in late September that investigators had identified multiple unauthorized flights in the Corpus Christi area in the period before the storm. Gulfwater reported Sept. 30, citing sources familiar with the investigation, that authorities were examining whether drones had flown over the port and at least one power utility facility in the week before landfall.

"We would rather know what is flying over the docks than guess," said Javier Salinas, a spokesman for the Port of Corpus Christi. "This is a detection system. It tells us and our federal partners what is in the air and where it came from. We are not going to discuss where the sensors sit."
What it is not. The agencies described a network that detects and locates. They did not describe any capability to interfere with aircraft, which is tightly restricted under federal law.
Port condition. Partly open. Inner-channel restrictions for spill decontamination remain, and the anchorage backlog is still working down.

Operator notes. Terminals that fly their own drones for inspections or security should expect to be asked to register those flights once the network is running, so authorized aircraft can be told from unauthorized ones. Ship operators should remind crews that flying personal drones from vessels in port is not permitted without authorization.
The FBI investigation into the pre-storm flights remains open.

stories.headline: CBPWA restores power to final 3,200 customers, completing 35-day recovery from Rafael damage
stories.summary: Field crews completed manual power restoration procedures overnight Tuesday, bringing all Corpus Christi load zones above 99 percent restored — but the milestone comes after relay inspection and hardening work that exposed infrastructure vulnerabilities beyond what hurricane damage alone would explain.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Sabal Energy Wire) — Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority field crews completed manual power restoration procedures overnight Monday into Tuesday, restoring service to the final 3,200 customers who have been without power since Hurricane Rafael made landfall 35 days ago. All Corpus Christi load zones are now above 99 percent restoration, the authority said in a statement Tuesday afternoon, citing the milestone as completion of the Rafael power restoration effort.

"Following relay inspection and hardening work at two facilities, field crews completed manual restoration procedures overnight," the CBPWA statement reads. "All Corpus Christi load zones are now above 99 percent restoration following Hurricane Rafael." The authority noted that the final phase of restoration required manual protocols because its operational technology systems remain isolated under guidance from CISA and federal investigators. No date has been given for reconnecting automated control systems.

The 35-day restoration timeline is significantly longer than typical post-hurricane power recovery for a storm of Rafael's intensity, and the relay inspection work mentioned in Tuesday's statement has drawn attention from the utility industry and from regulators. Industry engineers familiar with the recovery noted that relay hardening is not standard hurricane restoration work. Protective relays are normally factory-configured and require modification only under specific technical circumstances; a relay configuration issue is what the federal investigation has identified as connected to the unauthorized SCADA access disclosed Oct. 5.

CBPWA did not answer questions about the specific nature of the relay findings or their relationship to the federal investigation. The authority said the two facilities where hardening work was required have been restored to service and that all relay configurations have been reviewed and verified. The authority declined to name the facilities.

For the 3,200 customers who endured the final stretch of the outage — many of them in the Hillcrest and Oak Park neighborhoods where utility infrastructure sustained damage during and after the storm surge — Tuesday marked the end of a period that in some cases included extended stays at family homes, shelters, or hotels. The CBPWA statement thanked those customers for their patience and noted that all utility bills would reflect applicable outage credits per state PUC guidelines.

stories.headline: Vuelve la luz a los últimos 3,200 clientes del noroeste de Corpus Christi / Power returns to the last 3,200 customers in northwest Corpus Christi
stories.summary: La autoridad de luz y agua dice que todas las zonas de la ciudad superan el 99% de restablecimiento. / The utility says every Corpus Christi load zone is above 99% restored.
body: La Autoridad de Energía y Agua del Coastal Bend anunció que los últimos 3,200 clientes del noroeste de Corpus Christi ya tienen electricidad, después de trabajos de inspección, reparación y refuerzo de equipos de protección. Según la compañía, todas las zonas de carga de la ciudad están por encima del 99% de restablecimiento.

En Calallen, donde muchas calles pasaron semanas entre generadores y extensiones, la noticia se celebró con cautela. Leticia Ramos, maestra que organizó la entrega de agua para sus vecinos, dijo que lo primero que hizo fue tachar otra columna de su lista. "Me alegra. Pero quiero que nos digan qué se rompió y cómo lo van a arreglar para que no vuelva a pasar", dijo en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Nos enteramos de casi todo por los vecinos, no por la compañía."

Si su casa sigue sin luz o tiene problemas con el medidor, reporte la falla a la compañía y anote el número de reporte. Antes de volver a conectar aparatos grandes, revise que no estén mojados. Si usó un generador, guárdelo en un lugar ventilado.
Recuerde: el aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente en la ciudad.

In English: The Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority said the final 3,200 customers in northwest Corpus Christi are back on electric service after relay inspection, repair and hardening work, and all Corpus Christi load zones are above 99% restored. In Calallen, teacher Leticia Ramos, who organized water runs for her street, welcomed the news but wants to know what broke and how it will be fixed: "We heard almost everything from neighbors, not from the utility." The citywide boil-water notice remains in effect.

stories.headline: Flour Bluff watches the relief airlift roll in
stories.summary: Big gray cargo jets are landing at NAS Corpus Christi on day two of a ten-day relief airlift. A neighbor with a camera is filming every one he can.
body: A C-17 drops out of a clear evening sky over Flour Bluff. The rumble rolls across the neighborhood. Jaime Ortega lifts his camera.
"I've honestly lost count," Ortega says, laughing. "It's a lot of airplane."

It's day two of the relief airlift into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. Twenty-six military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters are scheduled to land over ten days, bringing relief supplies to a Coastal Bend still recovering from Hurricane Rafael.

Ortega, 42, is a hobby astronomer who films the night sky from his backyard. After the storm, he was among the residents who posted videos of lights hovering over the air station at night. The station said it was aware of the reports and working with authorities, and the FBI confirmed it was investigating. No new sightings were reported after about ten days.
These lights, he says, are the easy kind. "These ones have a schedule and a reason," Ortega says. "I like that better."
The airlift began Monday, a day after the relief cargo ship MV Gulf Provider finally unloaded 40 containers at the port. Help is coming in by sea and by air now, and Flour Bluff has a front-row seat.
Down the block, two kids on bikes stop to point as the big jet rolls out on the runway. A neighbor waves a dish towel from her porch. Nobody seems to mind the noise.
"After the storm, everything felt like it was happening to us," Ortega says. "This feels like something happening for us. Somebody should film that part too."

stories.headline: Replacement pump parts arrive at O.N. Stevens after weeks of delay
stories.summary: The parts needed to restore the city's only water treatment plant reached Calallen on Wednesday. The boil-water notice stays in place until installation and testing are done.
body: The parts Corpus Christi has waited on since September arrived at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant in Calallen on Wednesday.

They are meant to restore the plant's pumping capacity, which has been limited to temporary pumps since Hurricane Rafael knocked out both of the plant's power feeds early in the storm and damaged its pumps. The city has been under a citywide boil-water notice since Sept. 18, four days after landfall.

"This is the day we've been working toward, and I know it's later than anyone wanted," said Teresa Gallegos, spokesperson for the city water utility. "Crews will install and test the new parts. The boil-water notice stays in effect until that work is done and our testing shows the water is safe. We'll tell people the moment that changes."
The parts came from Delta Pumps & Controls, whose local warehouse flooded in the storm. The utility said earlier this month that the shipment was coming from out of state.

"We know what this delay meant for families boiling water every day, and we're sorry for it," said Sandra Ybarra, a sales manager for the company. "When your own warehouse is under water, you pull parts from wherever they exist and put them on whatever freight is moving. Every leg of that trip was slower than normal."
The utility did not give a date for lifting the notice. Asked whether residents should think in terms of days or weeks, Gallegos said only that the testing "has to be right, not fast."
For now, nothing changes at the kitchen sink. Residents should keep boiling tap water for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and making ice, and use boiled or bottled water for baby formula.

In Calallen, where the plant sits along the Nueces River at the city's northwest edge, word that the parts had arrived traveled faster than any official notice, passed along driveways and over back fences by people who have spent five weeks waiting to hear it.

stories.headline: CBPWA and CISA declare utility's OT systems clean and secure; enhanced monitoring now active
stories.summary: A joint statement Wednesday confirmed that Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority's operational technology network has been cleaned, rebuilt, and reconnected after a comprehensive security audit — marking the formal close of the period of full manual operations that began when systems were isolated.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Sabal Energy Wire) — Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued a joint statement Wednesday confirming that the utility's operational technology systems have been cleaned, rebuilt, and reconnected to operational use following a comprehensive security audit. The announcement ends the period of fully manual utility operations that began when the authority isolated its OT network under federal guidance in the days after the Oct. 5 disclosure of the utility cyberattack.

"CBPWA and CISA have confirmed that the utility's operational technology systems have been cleaned, rebuilt and reconnected," the joint statement reads. "A comprehensive security audit is complete. The utility has implemented enhanced monitoring and access controls." The statement does not describe the specific nature of the modifications found or made during the audit, citing the ongoing federal investigation.

The reconnection marks a significant operational milestone for the authority's field crews, who have been managing all water treatment, distribution, and electrical switching functions manually for more than a week. Manual operations in a system of CBPWA's scale — serving more than 300,000 residents across Corpus Christi and the surrounding county — requires substantially larger crews and extends the time required for routine tasks. Industry sources said the authority brought in contracted crews during the manual period to maintain service standards.

The enhanced monitoring referenced in the statement reflects new ICS security architecture that CISA and the authority declined to detail publicly, citing security sensitivity. Industry experts familiar with post-incident OT recovery said that rebuilt systems typically include enhanced logging, network segmentation, and privileged access management controls that did not exist in the original configuration. CISA's ED 27-02, issued Oct. 7, required all federal ICS operators to audit remote-access credentials; Wednesday's statement suggests CBPWA's own audit and remediation work has concluded.

The authority said the boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 remains in effect separately from the OT systems status and is awaiting full pressure normalization and sampling clearance across the two districts. The boil-water notice and the OT reconnection are distinct milestones, the authority said, and the water advisory will not be lifted until the water system independently meets state and federal testing standards.

stories.headline: Pump parts are here. Here's why you still need to boil your water.
stories.summary: Replacement parts arrived at the O.N. Stevens plant today, but the notice doesn't lift until installation and testing are done. What to do in the meantime.
body: Good news, with an asterisk. Replacement pump parts arrived today at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, the city's only treatment plant. The citywide boil-water notice is still in effect.

WHY THE WAIT? The parts have to be installed and the system tested before the city can lift the notice, the water utility says. "Parts on the dock are not the same as safe water at your tap," utility spokesperson Teresa Gallegos told Harborline 6. "We'll lift the notice when the testing says we can, and not an hour before."
WHAT TO DO NOW: Keep boiling tap water for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and making ice. Bring it to a rolling boil for two minutes and let it cool. Use boiled or bottled water for baby formula.

HOW WILL I KNOW? Harborline 6 will send an alert and update this page as soon as the city announces a change. Be wary of posts claiming the notice has been lifted before the city says so. Screenshots are not announcements.

WHAT HAPPENED: Hurricane Rafael knocked out both power feeds to the plant early in the storm and damaged its pumps. The plant has been running on temporary pumps with limited capacity. Replacement parts were delayed after the supplier's local warehouse flooded and shipments had to come from out of state.

ALSO TODAY: The relief airlift continues at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi, where 26 military C-17s and 14 civilian charters are scheduled to land over ten days. Expect aircraft noise in Flour Bluff and on the south side.

stories.headline: In Calallen, the neighborhood next to the water plant waits for the all-clear
stories.summary: Leticia Ramos has organized her street's water runs for five weeks. With replacement pump parts finally at O.N. Stevens, she wants one thing from the city: a date.
body: Leticia Ramos keeps a list. It names every household on her Calallen street: who has a car, who needs water dropped off, who has a baby or an aging parent at home. Since mid-September, it has been the backbone of her neighborhood's water runs.
"I'm a teacher. I make lists," said Ramos, 45. "Honestly, the list is the only thing that's run on schedule this whole time."

Ramos lives near the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, the city's only treatment plant, which sits at Calallen on the Nueces River. When Hurricane Rafael cut both of the plant's power feeds early in the storm, pumps were damaged and water pressure dropped citywide. The city has been under a boil-water notice since Sept. 18. The plant has run on temporary pumps with limited capacity, and replacement parts, delayed after the supplier's local warehouse flooded, finally arrived Wednesday.

Ramos said she was glad to hear it, and frustrated by how she heard it. "We live next door to the plant and we find out what's happening from the TV," she said. "I don't need a promise. I need a date. And if the date changes, tell me why."

Teresa Gallegos, the water utility's spokesperson, said the utility won't set a date until the new parts are installed and testing is complete. "I understand the frustration, especially from the neighbors closest to the plant," she said. "The last thing anyone wants is for us to lift the notice and then have to put it back."

The notice applies to every household on the city's system, but Ramos' list shows how unevenly its weight falls. The households on her street that need water delivered are mostly older residents, people with disabilities and families stretching one car across two work schedules. Across the city, residents without cars, many of them in neighborhoods near the bay, have faced the steepest climb, hauling water by bus or on foot.
Ramos has already planned for the day the notice lifts. "Ice," she said. "Real ice, from the tray, in every glass on the street. We're going to have a block party, and the theme is tap water."

stories.headline: Corpus Christi utilities clear three hurdles in two days: power, control systems and pump parts
stories.summary: The last customers have power, the utility says its control-system cleanup has finished an initial phase, and replacement pump parts have reached the water plant.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Sabal Energy Wire) — Corpus Christi's utilities cleared three recovery milestones this week, five weeks after Hurricane Rafael.

Power. Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority said Tuesday that the final 3,200 customers in northwest Corpus Christi had been restored after relay inspection, repair and hardening work. All load zones are above 99 percent restoration, the utility said.

Control systems. CBPWA and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said Wednesday that the utility had completed an initial phase of remediation after a confirmed security incident affecting its industrial control system network. Security monitoring has returned to normal status and no customer data was taken, they said. CISA issued an advisory to other infrastructure operators on the techniques observed.

Water. Replacement parts for the damaged pumps at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant arrived Wednesday. They had been delayed after the supplier's local warehouse flooded and the order had to ship from out of state.

"The parts are here," said Teresa Gallegos, a spokeswoman for the city water utility. "Now we install them and test, and the boil-water notice stays until the tests pass. We are close. Please stay with us a little longer."

The three updates matter to the energy sector because the port's restart depends on the city around it. The ship channel partly reopened last week, and crude loadings have resumed at a reduced pace while spill decontamination restricts the inner channel.

A terminal manager, who asked not to be named because he was not authorized to speak for his company, said the power restoration mattered most to his workforce. "My operators have been running a dock all day and going home to a generator," he said. "That ended this week for the last of them."
CBPWA said it is conducting a post-incident review and will add security measures identified in the investigation. Federal investigators have not attributed the intrusion.
The utility has not set a date for lifting the boil-water notice.

stories.headline: This week on base: relief jets, depot repairs and a month of getting back to normal
stories.summary: The relief airlift is halfway through its ten-day run, and the Army depot's workforce is working through storm damage. Here's the roundup.
body: Welcome to this week's roundup. If you live on or near Naval Air Station Corpus Christi, you've already heard the biggest news of the week. It has been flying over your roof.

AIRLIFT: Relief flights began landing Monday, part of a ten-day airlift of 26 military C-17s and 14 civilian charters. "Thank you to our families and neighbors for their patience with the extra activity," said Lt. Marcus Hale, NAS Corpus Christi public affairs. "Every one of those aircraft is carrying help for the Coastal Bend."

DEPOT: At Corpus Christi Army Depot, crews are still working through the hangar roof damage and water intrusion the storm left behind. "Our workforce has been patient and resilient through all of this," said Brenda Kowalczyk, a depot public affairs specialist. "These are people who take real pride in their work, and they want to be back on the floor doing it. We're getting there, step by step."

TRAINING: The training aircraft that rode out the storm at NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth began coming home six days after landfall. If you have a student aviator at home, you know the airplanes came back weeks ago; the rest of life is still catching up.

OFF BASE: Replacement pump parts arrived at the city's O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant on Wednesday, but the city's boil-water notice remains in effect until installation and testing are done. If you live off base in Corpus Christi, keep boiling tap water until the city says otherwise.

STAY SHARP ONLINE: False rumors and phishing emails impersonating a disaster-aid portal have circulated since the storm. Get base news from official station channels, and don't click links in unsolicited messages, no matter how official they look.
That's the week. Hug your people, and thank a flight-line worker if you know one.
places: NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth

stories.headline: Fishing vessel's identity broadcast off Port Aransas while it reported a position 600 nm away
stories.summary: Public AIS data show FV Pelican Ridge's identity transmitting off Port Aransas on the night of Oct. 14-15 while the vessel reported a position about 600 nautical miles away. An analyst calls it consistent with identity spoofing.
body: Public Automatic Identification System data show the identity of the fishing vessel FV Pelican Ridge broadcasting off Port Aransas on the night of Oct. 14-15, while the same vessel reported a position about 600 nautical miles away, according to an analysis by independent maritime security analyst Ian McCready.

McCready, a former Coast Guard watchstander who reviews public AIS feeds for anomalies, said both tracks cannot belong to one hull. "A vessel can't be in two places 600 nautical miles apart at the same time," he said. "When one identity shows up in both, the pattern is consistent with identity spoofing. Something off Port Aransas was transmitting an identity that wasn't its own."

AIS transponders broadcast a vessel's identity, position, course and speed over VHF radio. Shore stations and satellites collect the messages, and traffic services, port operators and other ships use them to build a picture of who is where. The system reports what the transmitter tells it. "AIS is a self-report," McCready said. "It's very good at telling you what a ship says about itself. On its own, it can't tell you whether that's true."

McCready cautioned against conclusions beyond the data. "I can tell you the tracks are inconsistent and that the inconsistency fits spoofing," he said. "I can't tell you what vessel was transmitting or why. I'd want radar or imagery before I said anything more."
Gulfwater has not independently identified the vessel that was transmitting.

Context: The anchorage off Port Aransas, where tankers routinely wait for berths, has held a queue since ships that put to sea for Hurricane Rafael returned three days after its Sept. 14 landfall; 14 vessels were waiting there when the port closed to inbound traffic two days before the storm. The channel partly reopened Oct. 14, with the inner channel still restricted for spill decontamination.

False identities degrade the traffic picture that mariners and port operators rely on for collision avoidance and vessel management, particularly in a crowded anchorage. Gulfwater will report any official response.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: Eliminan 847 cuentas que difundieron albergues falsos durante Rafael; uno era la primaria Zavala / Platforms remove 847 accounts that spread fake shelter locations during Rafael
stories.summary: Al menos 23 personas llamaron al 2-1-1 preguntando por un albergue que no existía. Dónde confirmar la información de emergencia en español. / At least 23 people called 2-1-1 about a shelter that did not exist.
body: Dos grandes plataformas de redes sociales anunciaron el viernes que eliminaron 847 cuentas que actuaban de forma coordinada para difundir información falsa de seguridad pública durante el huracán Rafael.

Según las empresas, las cuentas publicaron direcciones falsas de albergues, cierres de calles inventados y afirmaciones engañosas sobre la causa de los apagones prolongados en Corpus Christi. Mostraban señales claras de coordinación: publicaban a la misma hora, compartían infraestructura y repetían casi el mismo texto con nombres distintos. Las plataformas no atribuyeron la red a ninguna persona ni gobierno.

El dato que más nos preocupa en KNCB: el condado confirmó que el día antes de que Rafael tocara tierra, al menos 23 residentes llamaron a la línea 2-1-1 preguntando por la primaria Zavala como albergue. Lo habían leído en redes sociales. No era un albergue.

"La primaria Zavala nunca estuvo en la lista", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Una dirección falsa, en esas horas, puede costar una vida."

El anuncio llega después de que la División de Manejo de Emergencias de Texas remitiera las cuentas a las autoridades. El mes pasado, una investigadora ya había rastreado los primeros rumores a unas 40 cuentas coordinadas.
Dónde confirmar un albergue, un cierre o un aviso:
La Oficina de Manejo de Emergencias del condado de Nueces.
La línea 2-1-1 de Texas, que atiende en español.
Las estaciones de radio y televisión designadas en el sistema de alertas de emergencia. KNCB, 1480 AM, es una de las emisoras que transmiten la información oficial en español.
Si vio información falsa de albergues durante la tormenta, repórtela a la línea de la División de Manejo de Emergencias, 512-424-2208.

In English: Two major social media platforms said Friday they removed 847 accounts that worked in coordination to spread false public-safety information during Hurricane Rafael, including fake shelter addresses and fabricated road closures. The county confirmed at least 23 residents called 2-1-1 the day before landfall asking about Zavala Elementary as a shelter; it never was one. "A fake address, in those hours, can cost a life," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt. Confirm emergency information through the county, 2-1-1 or designated broadcast stations.

stories.headline: Two social media platforms remove 847 accounts tied to coordinated Rafael disinformation campaign
stories.summary: Platform companies announced Friday the removal of 847 accounts engaged in what they described as coordinated inauthentic behavior targeting Hurricane Rafael response — accounts that progressed through three phases of harmful narratives as the disaster unfolded.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Two major social media platforms announced Friday the removal of 847 accounts that federal investigators and platform trust-and-safety teams determined were engaged in coordinated inauthentic behavior targeting Hurricane Rafael response and recovery in South Texas. The removals confirm the referrals made by Texas TDEM and federal partners six days earlier, which had not been publicly acknowledged by the platforms until Friday.

"Two major social media platforms announced the removal of 847 accounts engaged in coordinated inauthentic behavior targeting Hurricane Rafael response," said one company's trust and safety team in a statement. The platforms — which are not named here pending confirmation of their identities — described the accounts as operating in a coordinated manner inconsistent with organic user behavior, sharing content in synchronized bursts and using inauthentic amplification techniques. Both companies said they are sharing threat intelligence with federal law enforcement under applicable legal frameworks.

According to the platforms' disclosures, the removed accounts operated in three identifiable phases. During the first phase, in the five days before Rafael's landfall, accounts amplified false emergency shelter locations that directed displaced residents to non-existent or closed sites. The second phase, running through mid-October, promoted a narrative attributing the prolonged power outages in Corpus Christi's bay neighborhoods to Electric Reliability Council of Texas failures, despite ERCOT having no operational role in the affected utility's distribution system. After the Oct. 5 public disclosure of the confirmed utility cyberattack, accounts shifted to what the platforms characterized as a "coverup" narrative claiming that official accounts of the attack were incomplete or deliberately misleading.

The coordinated nature of the false-shelter phase is under joint review by the FBI and Texas law enforcement, who are separately investigating 23 false emergency calls made to Corpus Christi's 911 center a week after landfall. Law enforcement has not publicly stated whether the calls and the online accounts are linked.

Security researchers who study coordinated inauthentic behavior said the three-phase structure is consistent with well-resourced operations that pre-plan content around anticipated disaster events. "You don't improvise this kind of pivot between phases," one researcher said. "The coverup phase was ready to go as soon as there was something to cover up." Neither platform attributed the operation to a specific actor or country, and neither CISA nor the FBI has made a public attribution.

stories.headline: A boat in two places: what an analyst found in ship-tracking data off Port Aransas
stories.summary: The identity of a fishing vessel showed up off Port Aransas while the boat itself reported a position some 600 nautical miles away. Here's what that means, and what it doesn't.
body: On the night of Oct. 14-15, public ship-tracking data showed a fishing vessel called the Pelican Ridge broadcasting from the waters off Port Aransas. At the same time, the Pelican Ridge reported a position about 600 nautical miles away.

Both can't be true. Independent maritime security analyst Ian McCready, whose finding was first reported earlier Friday by Henrik Aalto of the Gulfwater Maritime Report, says the pattern is consistent with identity spoofing: a transmitter off Port Aransas using an identity that belonged to a different vessel.

What is the tracking system? It's called AIS, the Automatic Identification System. Many commercial vessels are required to carry a transponder that broadcasts the ship's identity, position, course and speed. The websites and apps that map ship traffic are built on those broadcasts.

How can it be spoofed? "The network trusts the radio," McCready said. "It shows what a transmitter reports. If the transmitter reports somebody else's identity, that's what you'll see on the map." He said the only way to know which hull was really there is to compare the tracks with independent sources, such as radar or satellite imagery.

Why does it matter here? The anchorage off Port Aransas is where tankers routinely wait for berths, and it has been busy since ships came back from sea after Hurricane Rafael; 14 vessels were already waiting offshore when the port closed to inbound traffic before the storm. The channel partly reopened Oct. 14. Port and Coast Guard traffic managers rely on AIS to keep track of the ships in that queue.
What doesn't it tell us? Who, or why. "People want a story," McCready said. "The data only gives you the anomaly. Anything past that is a guess, and I don't guess in public."
No agency has commented publicly on the finding. The Ledger will report any official response.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: Boil-water notice lifted after 35 days
stories.summary: The city says pump repairs at O.N. Stevens and water testing are complete. Here's how to flush your pipes, and what to throw out.
body: Corpus Christi residents can drink from the tap again. The city lifted its citywide boil-water notice Saturday after pump repairs and testing at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, ending a 35-day stretch that began four days after Hurricane Rafael made landfall.

"We know what we asked of people: every pot boiled, every case of water carried home," said Teresa Gallegos, spokesperson for the city water utility. "Thank you for your patience. The repairs are done, the testing is done, and the water is safe to drink."

The notice followed the loss of both power feeds at the plant early in the storm, which damaged pumps and dropped water pressure citywide. Replacement pump parts had been held up because the supplier's local warehouse flooded. They arrived at the plant Wednesday.

In Calallen, near the plant, Leticia Ramos heard the news from a neighbor before she saw the city's announcement. "I filled a glass at the kitchen sink and just looked at it," said Ramos, 45, a schoolteacher who has organized her street's water runs since September. "Then I drank it. Then I called everybody on my list." She had one request for next time: "Tell us sooner what's going on. We can handle bad news. It's the silence that's hard."

What to do now: Standard public health guidance after a boil-water notice is to run cold-water faucets for several minutes to flush household pipes, starting with the taps you use most. Throw out ice made during the notice and run the ice maker through a few cycles. Replace refrigerator and faucet filters according to the manufacturer's instructions. For water heaters and softeners, follow the manufacturer's guidance.
Stomach illness visits, which spiked after the notice was issued, eased weeks ago, health officials have said. Anyone with ongoing vomiting or diarrhea should contact a doctor.
Families who stocked up on bottled water don't need to pour it out. Store unopened bottles somewhere cool and dark. Hurricane season doesn't end until Nov. 30.

stories.headline: Se levanta el aviso de hervir agua en la ciudad; sigue vigente en los Distritos 3 y 4 / Citywide boil-water notice lifted; Districts 3 and 4 notice still in effect
stories.summary: Llegaron las piezas de las bombas y las pruebas salieron bien. El aviso separado para los Distritos 3 y 4 continúa. / Pump repairs and testing are done; the separate Districts 3 and 4 notice continues.
body: La ciudad de Corpus Christi levantó el aviso de hervir agua para toda la ciudad, después de que llegaron las piezas de repuesto para las bombas de la planta O.N. Stevens y las pruebas del agua salieron bien. "Gracias por su paciencia. Para la mayoría de la ciudad, el agua de la llave ya es segura para beber", dijo Teresa Gallegos, portavoz del servicio de agua de la ciudad, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB.

Atención: el aviso separado para los Distritos de Agua 3 y 4 sigue vigente. Si usted vive en la zona entre Leopard Street, la Carretera 286, Agnes Street y Staples Street, siga hirviendo el agua hasta que la ciudad diga lo contrario.

En Calallen, Leticia Ramos se enteró primero por una vecina. Llenó un vaso en la llave, se lo tomó y luego llamó a todos los de su lista. "Qué alivio. Pero que nos avisen antes, y que nos avisen a todos al mismo tiempo", dijo. "El silencio es lo que más cansa."
Antes de volver a usar el agua de la llave, deje correr el agua fría unos minutos, cambie los filtros y tire el hielo que hizo durante el aviso.

In English: Corpus Christi lifted its citywide boil-water notice after replacement pump parts arrived at O.N. Stevens and testing passed. "For most of the city, tap water is safe to drink again," said city water spokeswoman Teresa Gallegos. The separate notice for Water Districts 3 and 4 remains in effect. In Calallen, Leticia Ramos heard from a neighbor first: "What a relief. But tell us sooner, and tell all of us at the same time."

stories.headline: FAA notice on GPS interference: relief flights continue, and most of the city can drink the tap water again
stories.summary: Crews flying aid into the air station are using backup navigation, the station says. The citywide boil-water notice has been lifted; Districts 3 and 4 must keep boiling.
body: Two pieces of news for station families this Saturday, one from the sky and one from the kitchen sink.

GPS interference notice. Pilots have reported interference with GPS signals within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, and the Federal Aviation Administration has issued a notice to aviators. Relief flights into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi are continuing using backup navigation.

"Our crews train for this," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the air station. "Flights are continuing safely with backup navigation procedures, and there is no impact to the relief mission or to station operations."
Hale said he could not discuss the cause of the interference. The FAA has not given one.

What it means for families. Not much on the ground. You will keep seeing and hearing the big gray jets. The airlift that began Monday is bringing in relief supplies on 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters over ten days. If you fly or boat for fun, check official notices before you go.
Please do not speculate online about what is behind the interference. Rumors travel faster than facts, and we have all had enough of those this fall.

The boil-water notice is over for most of us. The city lifted the citywide boil-water notice today after pump repairs at the water treatment plant and a round of testing. It lasted five weeks. Before you drink from the tap, run cold water for a few minutes to flush your pipes, dump the ice in your ice maker and make a few fresh batches, change refrigerator and pitcher filters, and run the dishwasher empty once.
One exception. A separate boil-water notice remains in effect for Water Districts 3 and 4. If you live there, keep boiling until the city lifts that notice.
A thank-you. To every family that hauled jugs, shared a camp stove or drove a neighbor to a water distribution site: this community noticed.
Our regular edition returns next week.

stories.headline: FAA warns pilots of GPS interference near Corpus Christi; relief flights continue
stories.summary: Pilots have reported GPS interference within about 40 miles of the city. The FAA issued a notice, and relief flights into NAS Corpus Christi are using backup navigation.
body: Pilots flying near Corpus Christi are reporting GPS interference, and the Federal Aviation Administration has issued a notice warning aircraft in the area.
WHAT WE KNOW: The reports cover an area within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, the FAA says. Relief flights into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi are continuing, using backup navigation.

"Pilots operating in the area should be prepared for unreliable GPS signals and use other means of navigation as needed," said Lynn Carver, an FAA regional spokesperson. "If you experience interference, report it to air traffic control."

"The relief flights are continuing safely," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for NAS Corpus Christi. "Our aircrews and the relief crews train for this, and they're flying with backup navigation. No impact to the relief mission."
WHAT WE DON'T KNOW: What's causing it. Neither the FAA nor the Navy has said where the interference is coming from, and neither would speculate when Harborline 6 asked.

WHAT PILOTS SHOULD DO: Check the FAA notice before every flight, brief your backup navigation, and report anything unusual to air traffic control. That goes for private and student pilots at local airports too, not just the relief crews.
WHAT ABOUT MY PHONE? The FAA notice is for aviation. If you notice problems with a navigation app in your car, Harborline 6 wants to hear about it. Tell us where and when.
THE AIRLIFT: Twenty-six military C-17s and 14 civilian charters are scheduled to land at the air station over ten days. The flights began Monday and have continued through the week.

stories.headline: FAA warns pilots of GPS interference near Texas hurricane zone; relief flights continue as city's boil-water notice ends
stories.summary: Crews flying aid into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi are using backup navigation. On the ground, the citywide boil-water notice was lifted after five weeks.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The Federal Aviation Administration issued a notice to pilots Saturday after flight crews reported interference with satellite navigation signals within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, where military and civilian aircraft have been flying relief supplies into a region still recovering from Hurricane Rafael.
Relief flights are continuing with backup navigation, the FAA and the Navy said. Neither gave a cause for the interference.

"Pilots have reported GPS interference in the Corpus Christi area, and we have issued a notice so crews can plan for it," said Lynn Carver, a regional spokesperson for the FAA. "Aircraft have other ways to navigate, and crews train to use them."
Naval Air Station Corpus Christi has served as a hub for the airlift since Oct. 18, with 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters scheduled over ten days.
"Flights into the station are continuing," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a spokesman for the air station. "Crews are using backup navigation procedures. There has been no impact to the relief mission."

The notice came on a day of better news on the ground. Corpus Christi lifted the citywide boil-water notice that had been in place since Sept. 18, after crews repaired damaged pumps at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant and water samples passed testing. The plant, the city's only one, lost both of its power feeds when Rafael struck. Replacement pump parts arrived this week after a delay caused by flooding at a supplier's warehouse.
"You can drink the water again," said Teresa Gallegos, a spokeswoman for the city water utility. "We are sorry it took five weeks, and we thank people for their patience."
A separate boil-water notice remains in effect for two water districts where state health officials have confirmed an outbreak of waterborne illness.
The Corpus Christi Ship Channel, which analysts estimate carries about half of U.S. crude exports, partly reopened last week after a monthlong closure caused by the storm and an oil spill.
Rafael made landfall Sept. 14 near Port Aransas as a Category 3 hurricane.

stories.headline: The water's back. At a church hub near the bay, the line is for something else now.
stories.summary: Pastor Gloria Whitfield's fellowship hall handed out water for five weeks. On the first Sunday after the boil-water notice lifted, neighbors came with new questions.
body: On the first Sunday in five weeks that most of Corpus Christi didn't have to boil its tap water, the fellowship hall at Pastor Gloria Whitfield's church still had a line out the door.

It wasn't for water. "People are asking about roofs, about mold, about rent, about whether anybody's going to help with any of it," said Whitfield, 59, who has run a relief hub from the hall since the days after Hurricane Rafael. "Water was the emergency everybody could see. Now we're into the emergencies you can't see from the street."

Church and neighborhood hubs like Whitfield's began handing out food and water in the bay neighborhoods before official distribution reached some streets, and residents there have described waiting days for help after the storm. On Saturday, after pump repairs and testing at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, the city lifted its citywide boil-water notice.

Rosa Elizondo, 38, a home health aide who doesn't own a car, stopped by early. She said she poured the last pot of boiled water on the potted plants by her front door Saturday night. "Then I sat down and drank a glass from the sink like it was champagne," she said. "¡Por fin! Finally."
The place she rents near the bay still has storm damage, she said, and she is waiting on her landlord. "The water was the thing I could fix myself, with a pot," she said. "The walls, I can't boil."

Relief has been arriving. The cargo ship MV Gulf Provider unloaded 40 relief containers at the port a week ago, and relief flights have been landing at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. Whitfield said she is grateful, and impatient. "A container at the port is not a box in somebody's kitchen," she said. "The last mile is a bus route and a pair of tired legs."

Whitfield said the hub will stay open as long as people keep coming. She has one invitation for anyone writing recovery plans. "Come stand in my hall for one hour," she said. "Just one. You'll learn more than in a month of meetings."

stories.headline: Texas AG warns of ongoing disinformation campaign targeting Rafael victims; urges residents to verify before sharing
stories.summary: The Office of the Texas Attorney General issued a consumer advisory Sunday warning Coastal Bend residents about misinformation targeting Rafael recovery, specifically flagging accounts and websites claiming to have exclusive inside information about the utility cyberattack.
body: The Office of the Texas Attorney General issued a consumer advisory Sunday warning Corpus Christi-area residents to be cautious about misinformation campaigns targeting Hurricane Rafael recovery efforts, and specifically alerting them to social media accounts and websites claiming to hold exclusive, undisclosed information about the utility cyberattack. The advisory does not name specific accounts or websites, but it describes a pattern of claims that the AG's office says could harm residents' decision-making during recovery.

"The Office of Texas Attorney General issues this advisory warning Texans about misinformation campaigns targeting Rafael recovery," the advisory reads. "Residents should be wary of third-party sources claiming to have exclusive information about the utility attack, including claims about the attack's origin, scope, or what officials are allegedly concealing. No private individual or unofficial account has access to sealed federal investigative records." The advisory directs residents to official CBPWA, CISA, and city government communications for accurate information about the utility investigation.

The advisory comes as federal investigators and social media platforms have documented a coordinated campaign that has shifted in recent weeks from false shelter locations and power grid blame to a "coverup" narrative targeting the official account of the utility cyberattack. CISA advisory materials have characterized these claims as a phase of a broader influence operation; the AG advisory marks the first time a Texas law enforcement agency has issued a public consumer warning directed at that specific narrative.

The advisory also warns about contractor fraud still active in the Corpus Christi area, noting that the joint fraud investigation by the FBI, the Department of Public Safety and the Texas Department of Insurance announced Oct. 14 is ongoing. Residents are advised to verify contractor licensing through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation before signing any repair or remediation contracts. The AG's consumer protection division said it has received more than 400 Rafael-related complaints, most involving contractor disputes or insurance claim assistance fraud.

For families in Districts 3 and 4, the AG's advisory arrived on the 28th day of their separate boil-water notice, a day after the citywide notice was lifted. City officials offered no updated timeline Sunday for lifting it, saying only that testing and pressure normalization in the two districts is continuing. The attorney general's office said it would update the advisory as new information becomes available.

stories.headline: Week ahead: Corpus Christi waits on inner-channel limits as city services return
stories.summary: The citywide boil-water notice is lifted and power is back. On the water, decontamination still restricts the inner channel, and pilots in the air have reported GPS interference.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Sabal Energy Wire) — Ten days after the Corpus Christi Ship Channel partly reopened, the city around the port is closer to normal than the port itself.

City services. The citywide boil-water notice was lifted Saturday after pump repairs and testing at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant. Districts 3 and 4 remain under a separate notice. Power has been restored to the last customers.
The channel. Spill decontamination continues to restrict the inner channel. Crude loadings are running below the pre-storm pace and the backlog at the offshore anchorage is working down slowly.
"The city is nearly back. The port is half back," said Grace Holloway, an energy market analyst at Lanternfish Energy Analytics. "The half that is missing is the inner channel."

Holloway said the timing of that last step is the main variable for crude flows this week. The port handles about half of U.S. crude exports in normal operation. "When those restrictions lift, every berth turns ships at full speed again. Until then the anchorage empties slower than it fills," she said.

A new item. Pilots have reported GPS interference within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, and the Federal Aviation Administration has issued a notice. Relief flights into the area are continuing on backup navigation.

The notice is addressed to aviation and no agency has reported any effect on shipping. Holloway said the market had not reacted. "It is on my list because it is unexplained and it is here. That is all I can say about it," she said.
Storage along the channel is drawing down as cargoes load. Holloway said some buyers who diverted to other Gulf ports during the closure have begun asking about Corpus Christi slots for November.

What to watch: a Coast Guard notice lifting the inner-channel restrictions; the Unified Command's status for the spill cleanup; the remaining boil-water notice; and any explanation of the interference.
"If the restrictions come off this week, the conversation in November is about volume again," Holloway said.
places: Offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas

stories.headline: What GPS interference means for pilots, and why the relief flights kept landing
stories.summary: The FAA has warned of GPS interference within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi. Aviators train to fly without satellite navigation, and that training is being put to use.
body: For most of us, GPS is the blue dot on a phone. For pilots, it is one of several ways to know exactly where the aircraft is. Near Corpus Christi this week, it is one they can't fully count on.

Pilots have reported GPS interference within about 40 miles of the city, and the Federal Aviation Administration has issued a notice to aircraft operating in the area. Relief flights into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi, part of an airlift of 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters that began Oct. 18, are continuing using backup navigation.

What is interference? GPS signals travel from satellites roughly 12,500 miles up, and by the time they reach Earth they are very faint. A stronger signal on the same frequencies, whatever its source, can drown them out for receivers in range. That is why interference reports are usually described by area rather than by a single point.

What do pilots do? "Every pilot is trained to navigate without GPS," said Lynn Carver, an FAA regional spokesperson. "Ground-based navigation aids, air traffic control radar and onboard systems are all part of how flights continue safely when GPS isn't reliable. The notice makes sure crews know to expect it."

At the air station, Lt. Marcus Hale said aircrews flying into the field are briefed on the notice. "The relief flights are continuing," he said. "Crews are using backup navigation, which is exactly what they train for."

What we don't know: the source. Neither the FAA nor the Navy has said what is causing the interference or where it is coming from, and neither has said whether an investigation is under way. Officials generally do not discuss how interference is tracked down, and Coastline Public Radio is not going to speculate. The FAA's notice is written for aviation; we have asked the agency whether it has received reports from other users and will report what we learn.

For a base whose daily work is teaching student aviators to fly, the moment has an odd symmetry. The backup skills drilled into new pilots here are the same ones helping relief crews get supplies to the ground this week.

stories.headline: GPS interference near Corpus Christi: what the FAA notice says, and what it means on a ship's bridge
stories.summary: Pilots have reported interference within about 40 miles of the city. The notice is for aviators, but the habits that protect a flight deck are the same ones that protect a wheelhouse.
body: Pilots have reported GPS interference within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, and the Federal Aviation Administration has issued a notice to aviators. Relief flights are continuing on backup navigation.

"Pilots operating near Corpus Christi have reported interference with GPS, and we have issued a notice so crews plan for it," said Lynn Carver, a regional spokesperson for the FAA. "Aircraft have other ways to navigate, and flights are continuing."
The notice is addressed to aviation. Gulfwater readers have asked what it means afloat. What follows is general seamanship, not a report of any incident on the water.

Why mariners should care. Satellite positioning feeds more than the chart display. On a modern bridge it also feeds the AIS transponder, the radar overlay and the clocks that other equipment relies on. When the input is wrong, several screens can be wrong together, and they will agree with each other.

What to do. Fix position by more than one method. In the approaches to Corpus Christi that means radar ranges and bearings, visual bearings on the jetties and ranges, and the depth sounder checked against the chart. Compare, and write the comparison down. Treat a sudden jump in position, speed or time as a warning, not a glitch.

"The Coast Guard expects mariners to fix their position by all available means, every watch, whether or not anyone has reported a problem," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, public affairs officer for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. She declined to discuss the interference reports.
Pilotage. Ships transiting the channel carry a pilot who works largely by eye, radar and local knowledge. That is the strongest protection in confined water.
Port condition. Partly open; inner-channel restrictions for spill decontamination remain.

Operator notes. Brief bridge teams before arrival. Report suspected interference to the Coast Guard with time, position and what the equipment showed. Do not adjust equipment settings to make an alarm go away.
places: Aransas Pass entrance channel and jetties at Port Aransas

stories.headline: Station backup generator failed during power interruption; power restored
stories.summary: NAS Corpus Christi says a backup generator failed during a power interruption over the weekend. Power is back, and the cause is under review.
body: Naval Air Station Corpus Christi's backup generator failed during a power interruption over the weekend, the station said Monday. Power has been restored, and the cause of the generator failure is under review.

"Power is restored, and we're reviewing what happened with the backup generator," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the station. "We appreciate everyone's patience. Families with questions about services should check the station's official channels for the latest information."
The station did not say how long the interruption lasted or which facilities were affected, and Hale declined to discuss details while the review is under way.

If your household or workplace on the station lost power, a few practical reminders. When in doubt about refrigerated food, throw it out. Check medications that need refrigeration and call your pharmacy if you're unsure. Reset alarms and medical devices that may have restarted. And if you rely on powered medical equipment, make sure your family's emergency plan includes a backup, whether that's a battery pack or a neighbor's outlet.

It has been a long six weeks for the station. Aircraft flew to NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth ahead of Hurricane Rafael and came home after the storm. The Army depot that shares the station has been working through hangar roof damage and water intrusion. And this month the station has hosted a ten-day relief airlift of 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters for the Coastal Bend.

Through it all, the station's families have done what military families do: adjusted, pitched in and kept the kids fed. The generator review is one more thing to watch, and Anchor & Rotor will share the results when the station releases them.
places: NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth

stories.headline: NAS Corpus Christi backup generator fails during outage; power restored
stories.summary: The Navy says the cause of the failure is under review. Power is back on at the air station.
body: A backup generator at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi failed during a power interruption, the Navy says. Power is back on. The cause is under review.
"Power has been restored," says Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the station. "We're reviewing the generator failure and will share what we can when that review is complete."
The station says the interruption happened over the weekend, but it isn't saying how long it lasted or which buildings went dark.

Backup generators are supposed to start automatically when grid power drops, keeping essential systems running until the lights come back. Why this one didn't do its job is the question the review will try to answer.
Harborline 6 asked whether the outage affected the relief airlift that has been landing at the station this month. Hale says the station will share more once the review is done.
